processes.name: Speak-up intake & triage
processes.summary: Single front door for every workplace concern (hotline, web portal, manager, HRBP, email, exit interview), logged in one case system and routed through a triage matrix to Employee Relations, Ethics & Compliance, Legal or Security with a severity rating and conflicts check. Good looks like every concern logged within 1 business day, acknowledged within 2, assigned to an unconflicted owner within 3, and Legal alerted the same day to anything touching accounting, securities, export control, bribery or an executive.
processes.owner: Ethics & Compliance (intake & triage), Employee Relations (HR-conduct matters), Legal (privilege & escalation)
processes.trigger: A concern is raised through any channel, including anonymous hotline/web reports, manager or HRBP referrals, exit interviews, survey comments that allege misconduct, or an external agency notice
outputs: Case record in the hotline/case system (channel, category, severity, location)
Acknowledgment to the reporter with non-retaliation statement
Triage decision: owning function and route (investigate, statutory committee, management resolution)
Documented conflicts check for the assigned handler
Escalation notices to Legal, CHRO and Audit Committee chair for Severity 1 and SOX matters
Referral to statutory channels (India IC, Taiwan GEEA/bullying process, Ontario program)
processes.sla: Log within 1 business day; acknowledge within 2 bd; triage and assign within 3 bd (Severity 1 same day)

steps.label: Concern raised via any channel
steps.detail: Employee, contractor or third party raises a concern by hotline, web portal, manager, HRBP, email or exit interview. Anonymous reporting is offered where lawful and the portal issues a report key for two-way follow-up.

steps.label: Route manager-received concern
steps.detail: Managers who hear a concern (even informally) submit it through the portal or to ER within 1 business day; they do not investigate, confront the subject or promise confidentiality. Harassment, fraud, safety and retaliation concerns can never be 'handled informally'.

steps.label: Log case & acknowledge reporter
steps.detail: Create the case with channel, date, country/site, allegation category from the taxonomy, people involved and the reporter's original words. Acknowledge within 2 business days, restating non-retaliation and how to add information.
steps.control: All channels feed one case system; no side trackers in HR inboxes

steps.label: Rate severity & apply triage matrix
steps.detail: Severity 1: imminent violence, officer/VP subject, accounting or audit fraud, export-control/sanctions breach, data exfiltration; Severity 4: interpersonal or management-style issues. Matrix routes HR conduct/harassment to ER, fraud/bribery/COI/SOX to E&C, insider threat and violence to Security, and executive, regulator or litigation matters to Legal.

steps.label: Legal, SOX or executive issue?
steps.detail: Legal reviews every Severity 1-2 case and any matter involving accounting, internal controls, securities, export control, FCPA, a government report or an officer/VP subject, and decides on privilege and Audit Committee notice.

steps.label: Open privileged matter & escalate
steps.detail: Legal opens the matter under privilege, notifies the Audit Committee chair of accounting/auditing complaints under SOX 301 procedures, and clocks the DOJ self-disclosure window (120 days from an internal report). Legal names the investigating function (E&C, Security or external counsel).

steps.label: Confirm HR-track handling
steps.detail: ER decides between formal investigation (ER-02), statutory committee process (ER-03), threat response (ER-07) or documented management resolution, and records the rationale for any no-investigation decision.

steps.label: Conflicts check & assign owner
steps.detail: Confirm the proposed handler has no reporting line, relationship or prior involvement with the parties; use an external investigator if the subject is VP+ or sits in HR, Legal or E&C. Assign the owner with target dates in the case system.
steps.control: Documented conflicts check before assignment

steps.label: Trigger statutory routes & interim steps
steps.detail: Refer sexual harassment complaints to the India IC, Taiwan GEEA/bullying procedure or Ontario program as applicable, and decide immediate interim measures (separation of parties, paid leave) where safety is at risk.

steps.label: Case handed to owning process
steps.detail: The case is live with an owner, SLA clock and linked process (ER-02, ER-03, ER-05 or ER-07), and the reporter gets a status update through the portal.

raci.activity: Audit Committee escalation of accounting/audit complaints

controls.control: Monthly reconciliation of ER trackers, HR inboxes and manager referrals to the case system so no concern sits outside it
Accounting, internal-control and auditing complaints flagged and reported to the Audit Committee chair within 5 business days
controls.evidence: Escalation log and Audit Committee minutes

controls.control: Conflicts check completed and recorded before any case is assigned
controls.evidence: Conflicts attestation in the case record

kpis.name: Intake-to-assignment time
kpis.why: Statutory clocks (India 3-month filing, Taiwan authority notice, DOJ 120-day window) start early; delay destroys evidence and trust

kpis.name: Acknowledgment within 2 business days
kpis.why: Fast acknowledgment is the strongest driver of reporters staying inside the internal channel

kpis.name: Reports per 100 employees
kpis.why: Very low volume signals distrust or poor awareness, not a clean culture

considerations: Route by risk, not by who owns the headcount: a harassment complaint against a finance director that mentions expense manipulation is a SOX matter first.
Train managers that knowledge is imputed to the company once they hear a concern; the most common failure is a manager 'keeping it informal' for weeks.
Exit interviews, engagement-survey verbatims and Glassdoor-style posts can contain allegations; build a rule that any named misconduct becomes a case.

Hotline vendors process data across borders: China reports need PIPL notice, separate consent (or a documented HR-necessity basis) and a PIPIA, and vendor staff in China should not have access to bulk US employee data (DOJ Data Security Program).
Do not promise absolute confidentiality; promise need-to-know handling, and never ask anonymous reporters to identify themselves.

variations.when: Report names an executive officer, director, or someone in HR, Legal or E&C
variations.how: Route directly to General Counsel and the Audit Committee chair, restrict case access to exclude implicated functions, and use an external investigator.

variations.when: Concern arrives as a government charge or regulator inquiry (EEOC/CRD, HRTO, labor bureau, SEC)
variations.how: Legal owns the matter, issues a litigation hold (ER-09) and manages all contact; ER flags the employee for retaliation monitoring.

variations.when: Anonymous report with too little detail to act on
variations.how: Request specifics through the portal's two-way messaging; close as 'insufficient information' after 30 days without response, documenting each attempt.

countries.us: SOX 301 requires audit committee procedures for confidential, anonymous submissions on accounting and auditing matters, and Rule 21F-17 bars any intake script or acknowledgment that discourages SEC reporting or requires notice to the company first. Treat a securities-fraud report as SOX 806 protected activity from the moment it is logged.
countries.us-ca: The FEHA policy must offer a complaint route that bypasses the direct supervisor and commit to timely, impartial investigation (2 CCR 11023), and the Labor Commissioner whistleblower hotline notice must be posted (LC 1102.8). Adverse action within 90 days of a whistleblower or wage complaint is presumed retaliatory (LC 1102.5, SB 497).
countries.ca: Ontario's OHSA harassment program must include an alternative reporting channel when the supervisor is the alleged harasser, and every complaint must be investigated (s.32.0.7); BC WorkSafeBC policies require written reporting procedures. Criminal Code s.425.1 makes retaliation against employees who report offences to authorities a crime.
countries.in: Sexual harassment complaints by women must go to the office's Internal Committee (POSH Act s.9, filed within 3 months, extendable by 3), not be resolved by the hotline team, and worker grievances can go to the GRC (IR Code s.4). The global hotline should double as the Companies Act s.177 vigil mechanism.
countries.tw: Sexual harassment complaints trigger GEEA duties, including notifying the local labor authority of the complaint and outcome, and from 1 July 2026 workplace bullying complaints must be registered in MOL's reporting system. Complaints against the highest-ranking responsible person can be filed directly with the local authority.
countries.cn: The Women's Rights Law (2022) Art. 25 requires a sexual-harassment complaint channel, and hotline data sent to a US vendor needs PIPL notice, a cross-border transfer basis and a PIPIA (PIPL Arts. 38-39, 55). Keep intake records in Chinese where they may later be used as arbitration evidence.

processes.name: Workplace investigation
processes.summary: Fact-finding process for misconduct allegations (harassment, discrimination, retaliation, bullying, policy breaches, integrity issues) from scoping through findings, corrective action, closure and retaliation monitoring. It runs to one global method (T-INVESTIGATION, preponderance standard) with country overlays for Ontario OHSA, India POSH, Taiwan GEEA/bullying rules, China handbook-based discipline and US NLRA limits. Good looks like impartial investigators, evidence preserved before anyone is notified, findings per allegation within 30 days for standard cases, and outcomes that are consistent and survive challenge.
processes.owner: Employee Relations (process & quality), Legal (privilege, external investigators, high-risk matters), HRBP & Manager (interim measures and outcomes)
processes.trigger: Case assigned from ER-01 triage for formal investigation, a referral from a statutory committee, or a Legal instruction following a demand letter or agency charge
outputs: Investigation plan with allegations, scope, witnesses and statutory deadlines
Evidence index with chain-of-custody log
Interview records (signed or confirmed)
Investigation report with findings per allegation (T-INVESTIGATION)
Written closing letters to complainant and respondent
Corrective-action decision and non-retaliation monitoring record
processes.sla: Plan within 3 business days of assignment; standard investigations closed within 30 calendar days, complex within 60; statutory deadlines override (e.g., India IC 90 days)

steps.label: Receive triaged case from ER-01
steps.detail: Investigator reviews the intake record, severity and conflicts check, confirms a formal investigation is warranted and opens the investigation file from T-INVESTIGATION.

steps.label: Scope allegations & plan
steps.detail: Write each allegation as a discrete, testable statement tied to the policy clause breached, then plan witnesses, documents, electronic sources and interview order. Record jurisdiction deadlines (India IC 90 days, Taiwan authority notices, Taiwan Art. 12 30-day clock, CA 90-day retaliation window).

steps.label: Privilege or external investigator?
steps.detail: Legal decides whether counsel directs the investigation for privilege (executive subject, likely litigation, government reporting, whistleblower retaliation) and whether an external investigator is needed (VP+ subject, HR/Legal implicated, repeat respondent, or an Ontario inspector order).

steps.label: Engage external investigator
steps.detail: Legal retains the investigator under an engagement letter addressed to counsel that fixes scope, deliverable (oral or written report), timeline and data-handling terms (PIPL and DPDP clauses for Asia matters). ER stays the coordination point for logistics and interim measures.

steps.label: Implement interim measures
steps.detail: Put in place proportionate measures that do not disadvantage the complainant: schedule or reporting-line changes, remote work, no-contact instructions, or paid administrative leave for the respondent. Document the rationale; in China avoid unpaid suspension unless the handbook allows it.
steps.control: Retaliation-risk review of every interim measure affecting the complainant

steps.label: Preserve evidence before notice
steps.detail: Security/IT preserves mailboxes, Slack/Teams, repositories, DLP logs, badge data and device images before the respondent is notified; Legal issues a litigation hold (ER-09) if claims are reasonably anticipated. Log every collection in the chain-of-custody record.
steps.control: Chain-of-custody record for each collected source

steps.label: Notify parties in writing
steps.detail: Tell complainant and respondent the process, investigator, expected timeline, right to provide evidence and witnesses, and non-retaliation duty. Give the respondent enough detail to respond, and make any confidentiality request narrow and justified (NLRA).

steps.label: Interview parties & witnesses
steps.detail: Two-person interviews (investigator and note-taker), Upjohn warning when counsel-led, open questions before specifics, and a full opportunity for the respondent to answer every allegation and exhibit. Use independent interpreters, confirm notes with the interviewee, and never record in California without all-party consent.
steps.control: Upjohn warning documented in counsel-led interviews

steps.label: Review electronic evidence
steps.detail: Targeted review of company systems only, within the disclosed monitoring policy and privacy notices, using Legal-approved search terms and date ranges. China-origin data stays in China unless a PIPL transfer basis and Legal approval exist; personal social media is off limits in CA (LC 980).

steps.label: Weigh evidence & credibility
steps.detail: Apply the preponderance standard ('more likely than not') to each allegation using plausibility, corroboration, consistency, motive and detail; demeanor is a minor factor. Conclude substantiated, not substantiated or inconclusive per allegation.

steps.label: Write investigation report
steps.detail: Report per T-INVESTIGATION: allegations, scope, process, evidence summary, credibility analysis, findings per allegation and policy conclusion, with exhibits indexed. Legal reviews before finalization; counsel-directed reports carry privilege markings.

steps.label: Any allegation substantiated?
steps.detail: Legal and ER confirm findings are supported by the evidence and consistent with precedent cases before outcomes are decided.

steps.label: Decide outcome & remediation
steps.detail: Manager and HRBP, calibrated by ER, decide corrective action under ER-04 in proportion to findings and precedent. Add remediation for the complainant (restored opportunities, changed reporting line) and the team (training, manager coaching).

steps.label: Send closing communications
steps.detail: Tell both parties in writing that the investigation is complete and whether allegations were substantiated. Share corrective action with the complainant as local law requires (Ontario: results and corrective action in writing to both) and otherwise only at the level needed, and repeat the non-retaliation reminder.
steps.control: Closure letters issued within 5 bd of the outcome decision

steps.label: Monitor for retaliation
steps.detail: Check in with the complainant and key witnesses at 30, 60 and 90 days, and require ER review of any adverse action against them (rating, assignment, termination) for 12 months.

steps.label: Close case & retain file
steps.detail: Close the case with category, outcome and root cause; store plan, notes, evidence index, report and letters in restricted document management under the retention schedule and any active hold.

raci.A: Head of Employee Relations (General Counsel if privileged)

controls.control: Independence and conflicts check completed before an investigator is assigned; VP+ and HR/Legal subjects go external
controls.evidence: Conflicts attestation in the case file

controls.control: Evidence preserved with chain of custody before any party is notified
Legal review of report and findings before outcome decisions
controls.evidence: Legal sign-off recorded in the case system

controls.control: Statutory deadline tracker (India IC 90 days, Taiwan authority notices and Art. 12 clock, Ontario written results)
Adverse action against a complainant or witness within 12 months requires ER and Legal approval
controls.evidence: Darwinbox protected-activity flag and approval record

controls.control: Quarterly QA of a sample of closed cases for timeliness, documentation and consistency of outcomes across countries and levels

kpis.name: Median days assignment to closure letter
kpis.why: Delay erodes evidence and credibility, and in Taiwan can forfeit Art. 12 dismissal rights

kpis.name: Statutory deadlines met
kpis.why: Missed POSH or GEEA deadlines bring fines and undermine the defense

kpis.name: Substantiated retaliation claims after an investigation
kpis.why: Retaliation is the claim most likely to succeed even when the original complaint fails

kpis.name: Outcome consistency
kpis.target: No unexplained variance by country, level or demographic in quarterly QA
kpis.why: Inconsistent discipline is the main evidence in discrimination claims

kpis.name: Repeat respondents
kpis.target: < 5% with a new substantiated finding within 24 months
kpis.why: Tests whether corrective actions actually change behavior

considerations: Preponderance means 'more likely than not'; do not import a criminal standard or require eyewitness corroboration, since most harassment happens without witnesses.

Privilege is a trade-off: if the company will rely on the investigation as its Faragher/Ellerth defense, privilege over the report may be waived, so decide at the start which document is the business record.

Confidentiality directives: under Stericycle (still binding), blanket 'do not discuss' rules can violate NLRA Section 7; use case-specific justifications (evidence integrity, witness protection), time-limit them, and state that they never restrict reporting to the SEC, EEOC or NLRB (verify current Board standard given GC 26-04).

Allegations involving trade secrets or controlled technology need Trade Compliance input on who may review the evidence; releasing EAR-controlled design data to a foreign-person investigator can itself be a deemed export.

In China, brief counsel on state-secret and Counter-Espionage Law sensitivities, keep evidence onshore by default, and take signed Chinese-language statements because arbitration panels need Chinese evidence.
Interview in the witness's strongest language with an independent interpreter (never a colleague of the parties) and record the interpreter's name in the file.

Watch the discipline clock: Taiwan Art. 12 summary dismissal must follow within 30 days of learning the facts, and delayed action in China weakens an Art. 39 dismissal, so document the date management 'knew'.
Remote interviews: verify identity, ask the interviewee to confirm no one else is present, and prohibit recording by either side unless all parties consent.

variations.when: Respondent is an executive officer or director
variations.how: Audit Committee or Board chair oversees, external counsel investigates, and Legal assesses Code waiver, 8-K and clawback (POL-06) implications; Comp Committee is briefed on outcomes.

variations.when: Sexual harassment complaint by a woman in India
variations.how: The Internal Committee conducts the inquiry under ER-03 (90-day inquiry, report within 10 days, employer action within 60); ER supports with templates but cannot direct findings.

variations.when: Sexual harassment or bullying complaint in Taiwan
variations.how: Run under GEEA or the OSH Act bullying chapter: notify the local authority, register bullying cases in MOL's system, and use an investigation committee with external members where required.

variations.when: Complaint in Ontario
variations.how: Investigate under the OHSA harassment program and give both parties written results and corrective action; an inspector may order a third-party investigation at the employer's cost.

variations.when: Suspected data exfiltration by a current employee
variations.how: Security leads covert preservation before any notice, Legal assesses TRO or law-enforcement referral, and the exit path follows ER-10.

variations.when: Complainant withdraws or declines to participate
variations.how: Continue where there is risk to others or pattern evidence and document the decision; in India, conciliation only at the complainant's request and never with a monetary settlement.

variations.when: Unionized employees (US) or China union context
variations.how: US: honor Weingarten requests for a representative in investigatory interviews that may lead to discipline. China: notify the union before any resulting unilateral termination (LCL Art. 43).

countries.us: Prompt, impartial, documented investigations underpin the Faragher/Ellerth defense; the EEOC rescinded its 2024 harassment guidance in January 2026, but Title VII, Bostock and state-law coverage are unchanged. While Stericycle remains binding, blanket confidentiality instructions to witnesses risk NLRA Section 7 violations, and no instruction may impede reporting to the SEC (Rule 21F-17). Keep records through final disposition once a charge is filed (29 CFR 1602.14), and allow Weingarten representation for unionized employees.
countries.us-ca: 2 CCR 11023 requires timely, impartial investigation by qualified personnel, documented findings and appropriate remedial options, and CRD claims can be filed for 3 years (Gov Code 12960). Recording interviews needs all-party consent (Penal Code 632) and personal social media access cannot be demanded (LC 980). Any adverse outcome for a complainant within 90 days of protected activity carries the SB 497 retaliation presumption, so Legal reviews it.
countries.ca: Ontario OHSA s.32.0.7 requires an investigation appropriate in the circumstances of every harassment incident or complaint, and written notice to both the complainant and the alleged harasser of the results and any corrective action; an inspector can order a third-party investigation at the employer's cost (s.55.3). BC requires investigation under written bullying and harassment procedures with a reasonable response aimed at fully addressing the incident. Keep device and account searches proportionate: intrusion upon seclusion is actionable in Ontario, and BC PIPA requires reasonable purposes and notice.
countries.in: The Internal Committee handles sexual harassment complaints by women: inquiry within 90 days, report within 10 days, employer action within 60 days, with interim relief and strict confidentiality (POSH Act ss.11-13, 16). For other misconduct by 'workers', major penalties need a domestic enquiry (charge sheet, enquiry officer, hearing with cross-examination, report, second show-cause), or dismissal can be reversed with back wages. Forensic reviews can rely on DPDP s.7(i) employment purposes, with notice through policy and data minimization.
countries.tw: GEEA harassment complaints require immediate and effective corrective measures, an impartial investigation (MOL expects about 2 months, extendable by 1; verify) and notification of the complaint and outcome to the local labor authority. The OSH Act bullying chapter in force from 1 July 2026 adds interim protection, mediation where appropriate, investigation committees with at least half external members where required, MOL case registration, and fines of NT$30,000-750,000. If Art. 12 summary dismissal may follow, act within 30 days of learning the facts.
countries.cn: Discipline after an investigation holds up only if the breached rule is in a handbook adopted through democratic procedure (LCL Art. 4) and acknowledged by the employee, so cite the handbook clause in the report. Collect only necessary data under a PIPL notice, keep evidence onshore unless a transfer pathway exists, and take signed Chinese statements. Notify the union before any resulting unilateral termination (LCL Art. 43).

processes.name: Harassment complaints (statutory committees)
processes.summary: Runs the statutory complaint machinery that sits alongside ER-02: India's POSH Internal Committee, Taiwan's GEEA sexual-harassment and OSH Act bullying procedures with authority notification, China's Women's Rights Law complaint system and Ontario's OHSA harassment program. Good looks like committees constituted and trained before they are needed, statutory clocks never missed, filings made on time, and outcomes aligned with the global investigation standard.
processes.owner: Employee Relations (process), country HR leads (committee administration), Legal (statutory notifications & filings)
processes.trigger: A harassment or bullying complaint in a jurisdiction with a statutory committee or authority-notification regime (from ER-01), plus the annual committee and program maintenance cycle
outputs: Committee membership register and displayed notices (India IC, Taiwan committee)
Complaint register with statutory deadline tracking
Committee inquiry report and recommendations
Authority notifications and filings (Taiwan local authority, MOL bullying system, India annual report)
Annual program review record (Ontario OHSA, BC policy)
processes.sla: India: inquiry 90 days, report 10 days, employer action 60 days; Taiwan: authority notification per GEEA rules; Ontario: written results at close

steps.label: Complaint filed with committee
steps.detail: Complainant files in writing with the India IC (within 3 months of the incident, extendable by 3), the Taiwan harassment or bullying channel, the China complaint channel or the Ontario program; oral complaints are reduced to writing with help.

steps.label: Register & start statutory clock
steps.detail: Log with a jurisdiction flag so the tracker computes statutory dates, confirm committee quorum, and replace any conflicted member from the reserve list.
steps.control: Statutory deadline tracker opened for every complaint

steps.label: Make authority notifications
steps.detail: Taiwan: notify the local labor authority of the harassment complaint (and later the outcome) and register bullying cases in MOL's system from 1 July 2026; complaints against the highest-ranking responsible person can be filed directly with (and for bullying are handled by) the local authority. Other countries: log for annual reporting.

steps.label: Conciliation or mediation chosen?
steps.detail: India allows conciliation only at the complainant's request and never with a monetary settlement (POSH s.10); Taiwan bullying rules encourage mediation where appropriate. Otherwise proceed to formal inquiry.

steps.label: Grant interim relief
steps.detail: On committee recommendation, transfer either party, grant leave (up to 3 months in India, s.12) or remove the respondent's supervisory authority over the complainant, without loss of pay or opportunity for the complainant.

steps.label: Committee inquiry & report
steps.detail: The committee inquires using the T-INVESTIGATION method plus statutory steps: complaint copy to the respondent (India: within 7 working days, reply within 10; verify), hearings under natural justice, and external members where Taiwan bullying rules require. Written findings and recommendations follow (India: within 10 days of completion).

steps.label: Implement recommended action
steps.detail: Manager and HRBP, with ER, act on the committee's recommendations within statutory windows (India: 60 days) through ER-04; any departure needs Legal sign-off and written reasons.

steps.label: Close, notify & file returns
steps.detail: Send written outcomes to both parties (Ontario requires results and corrective action in writing), notify the Taiwan authority of the outcome, and include the case in the India IC annual report to the District Officer and the Board's report POSH disclosures.
steps.control: Statutory filings calendared with receipts retained

steps.label: Close case & feed program review
steps.detail: Close the case, schedule 30/60/90-day retaliation check-ins, and feed trends into the annual program and policy review.

controls.control: Quarterly composition check: India IC (senior woman presiding officer, external member, at least half women, 3-year terms) and Taiwan committee external members
controls.evidence: Membership register, appointment letters, displayed notices

controls.control: Deadline tracker escalates to Legal at 75% of any statutory period
Authority notification and annual filing checklist completed per case and per year
controls.evidence: Filing receipts and annual report copies

kpis.name: Statutory deadlines met
kpis.why: Missed POSH or GEEA deadlines bring fines and weaken any later defense

kpis.name: Committee members trained before first case and annually
kpis.why: Untrained committees produce reports that fail natural-justice review

kpis.name: Median days complaint to committee report (India)
kpis.why: Leaves margin inside the 90-day statutory limit

considerations: Run the statutory process and the global standard together: ER equips the committee with templates and legal support but cannot direct its findings.
India needs an IC for each office or administrative unit with 10+ employees, with a paid external member who is genuinely independent; a single global hotline does not satisfy POSH.
Build the Taiwan path for complaints against the highest-ranking responsible person (direct to the local authority) into the policy before it is needed.
Conciliation must never be used to pressure a complainant to drop a complaint, and POSH bars monetary settlement.
POSH protects women only; route complaints by men or non-binary employees through ER-02 under the global anti-harassment policy with the same rigor.

variations.when: Complaint against the Taiwan country manager or highest-ranking responsible person
variations.how: The complaint can be filed directly with the local authority (bullying cases are handled by it); HQ Legal manages the response and appoints an external investigator.

variations.when: Complainant or respondent is a contractor, intern or visitor
variations.how: India POSH covers aggrieved women at the workplace including visitors; coordinate with the vendor's IC or HR for vendor staff and record who leads.

variations.when: Ontario or BC complaint
variations.how: Run under the OHSA program or WorkSafeBC procedures, give written results to both parties, and log for the annual program review.

countries.us: No statutory committee; complaints run through ER-02 under Title VII and state law, with NY, IL, CT, DE and ME imposing policy or training duties. Sexual harassment claims cannot be forced into pre-dispute arbitration (EFAA 2022).
countries.us-ca: No committee, but 2 CCR 11023 requires a complaint process with alternatives to the direct supervisor and timely, impartial investigation; harassment training is 2 hours for supervisors and 1 hour for others every 2 years (Gov Code 12950.1).
countries.ca: Ontario OHSA ss.32.0.6-32.0.8 require a harassment program covering reporting, investigation, confidentiality and written results to both parties, including virtual harassment since October 2024, reviewed at least annually. BC bullying and harassment policies and procedures must also be reviewed annually.
countries.in: Each office with 10+ employees needs an IC (senior woman presiding officer, 2+ employee members, 1 external member, at least half women, 3-year terms) with details displayed in English and Kannada; fines run up to INR 50,000. The IC files an annual report to the District Officer, and the Board's report must disclose POSH complaint statistics.
countries.tw: GEEA (2024 amendments) requires a complaint channel at 10+ employees and published prevention measures, complaint procedures and disciplinary rules at 30+, with complaints and outcomes notified to the local authority. The OSH Act bullying chapter (1 July 2026) adds a parallel regime with MOL case registration, external investigators and fines of NT$30,000-750,000.
countries.cn: The Women's Rights Law (2022) Art. 25 requires rules, training, a complaint channel, prompt investigation and handling, and anti-retaliation, with no mandated committee. Any disciplinary outcome must rest on handbook rules adopted through democratic procedure.

processes.name: Corrective action & discipline
processes.summary: Turns substantiated findings and conduct issues into proportionate, documented and locally enforceable corrective action, from coaching through written and final warnings to dismissal. Good looks like consistent outcomes for like conduct across countries and levels, every action traceable to a policy clause and evidence, and local due-process steps (China handbook rules, Taiwan Art. 12 clock, India show-cause and domestic enquiry) completed before action.
processes.owner: Manager (decision), HRBP (process), Employee Relations (consistency & quality), Legal (dismissal-level review)
processes.trigger: Substantiated finding from ER-02/ER-03, or a manager-observed conduct, attendance or policy breach
outputs: Corrective-action recommendation with precedent comparison
Show-cause notice or charge sheet where required (India, China)
Signed warning or discipline letter (local language where needed)
Employee response and any appeal outcome
Darwinbox discipline record with expiry and eligibility flags
processes.sla: Decision within 10 business days of a finding; Taiwan Art. 12 dismissals within 30 days of learning the facts

steps.label: Conduct issue or finding received
steps.detail: Manager receives a substantiated finding from ER-02/ER-03 or observes a conduct issue, and takes no unilateral action beyond immediate safety steps.

steps.label: Classify & check precedent
steps.detail: Classify severity under the POL-13 matrix (minor, serious, gross misconduct) and pull precedent outcomes for similar conduct from the last 3 years. Check protected-activity flags (complaint, leave, whistleblowing or pay complaint in the last 90 days) before recommending anything.
steps.control: Protected-activity check before any recommendation

steps.label: Confirm local due-process path
steps.detail: India 'workers': show-cause and domestic enquiry for major penalties. China: the rule must be in the democratically adopted handbook. Taiwan: the rule must be in the filed work rules, and the Art. 12 30-day clock is running. California: 90-day retaliation presumption.

steps.label: Issue show-cause / hear employee
steps.detail: Put the specific allegations and evidence to the employee and give a real opportunity to respond (a written show-cause notice in India; a documented meeting elsewhere). Record the response and revisit the recommendation if new facts emerge.

steps.label: Dismissal or high-risk action?
steps.detail: Dismissal, demotion, or a final warning for an employee with a protected-activity flag goes to Legal; other actions are finalized by the manager and HRBP.

steps.label: Review dismissal case
steps.detail: Legal reviews evidence, statutory ground (China Art. 39, Taiwan Art. 12, India standing orders and enquiry report), timing and union notice (China LCL Art. 43), then hands dismissals to OF-02 for execution.
steps.control: Legal sign-off on every dismissal for cause

steps.label: Deliver corrective action
steps.detail: Manager and HRBP deliver the outcome in a meeting with a letter stating the conduct, policy clause, expected standard, consequence of recurrence and appeal route; local-language version in China and Taiwan.

steps.label: Acknowledge & optionally appeal
steps.detail: Employee signs acknowledgment of receipt (not agreement) by e-signature and may submit a written response or appeal within 5 business days to the manager-once-removed or ER.

steps.label: Record action & set review
steps.detail: Record type, date and expiry (e.g., written warning active 12 months) in Darwinbox and update bonus, promotion and rehire flags. Karnataka IT-exemption users report suspensions and dismissals to the Deputy Labour Commissioner.
steps.control: Discipline recorded in HRIS within 3 bd of delivery

steps.label: Closed & tracked for consistency
steps.detail: ER adds the action to quarterly consistency analytics (country, level, gender, age band) and closes the linked case.

raci.activity: Local due-process steps (show-cause, enquiry, union notice)

controls.control: Protected-activity and retaliation screen before any recommendation
controls.evidence: Completed checklist in the case record

controls.control: Legal approval for dismissals for cause and final warnings on flagged employees
controls.evidence: Approval record in the case system

controls.control: Quarterly review of outcome consistency by country, level and demographic group

kpis.name: Days from finding to decision
kpis.why: Protects the Taiwan 30-day window and the credibility of the process

kpis.name: Actions overturned on appeal, arbitration or in court
kpis.why: Measures whether local due process is actually followed

kpis.name: Unexplained outcome variance
kpis.why: Inconsistency is the core evidence in discrimination claims

considerations: Progressive discipline is the default, not a contract: US handbooks should preserve at-will status, while in China, Taiwan, India and Canada the documented steps are the evidence you need.
A global Code of Conduct alone is not enforceable in China or Taiwan; list serious violations concretely in the local handbook or filed work rules.
Keep performance and conduct separate: performance gaps go to PD-03, and labelling them misconduct invites reversal.
After Muldrow (2024), transfers and assignment changes used as discipline need documented legitimate reasons.
Executive misconduct may bear on clawback (POL-06) and disclosure, so loop in Legal early.

variations.when: Issue is performance, not conduct
variations.how: Route to PD-03 (PIP) with objective standards and support; in Taiwan and China this builds the Art. 11(5) / Art. 40(2) incompetence record.

variations.when: Executive officer misconduct
variations.how: Board or Comp Committee decides, with Legal assessing clawback, Code waiver and 8-K implications.

variations.when: Suspension pending domestic enquiry (India)
variations.how: Pay subsistence allowance under the standing orders (traditionally 50% for the first 90 days, then 75%; verify) and keep the suspension short and documented.

countries.us: At-will, but consistent, documented discipline is the main defense to discrimination and retaliation claims. Never discipline for Section 7 activity such as discussing pay or group complaints (NLRA; Stericycle).
countries.us-ca: Legal reviews any action within 90 days of wage, whistleblower or equal-pay protected activity (SB 497; up to $10,000 per LC 1102.5 violation), and lawful off-duty conduct and off-duty cannabis use cannot be disciplined (LC 96(k), Gov Code 12954). Keep a human decision-maker where any automated tool informs discipline (CRD ADS rules).
countries.ca: Just cause requires proportionality (McKinley), and Ontario ESA notice and severance are forfeited only for wilful misconduct, disobedience or wilful neglect of duty, so warnings and a real chance to improve are essential. Unpaid suspension without a contractual right risks constructive dismissal (Potter).
countries.in: Major penalties for 'workers' need a domestic enquiry (charge sheet, enquiry officer, hearing with cross-examination, report, second show-cause, reasoned order) or they can be reversed with back wages. Karnataka IT-exemption users must report suspensions, discharges and dismissals to the Deputy Labour Commissioner.
countries.tw: Only conduct listed in the filed work rules can be disciplined, penalties must be proportionate, and LSA Art. 12 summary dismissal must occur within 30 days of learning the facts. Courts apply the last-resort principle to anything short of gross misconduct.
countries.cn: Art. 39(2) serious-violation dismissals fail unless the rule is concretely defined in a handbook adopted through democratic procedure (LCL Art. 4) and acknowledged by the employee. The union must be notified before any unilateral termination (LCL Art. 43).

processes.name: Whistleblower & hotline case management
processes.summary: Operates the global hotline as the company's SOX 301 channel: accounting and auditing complaints reach the Audit Committee, anonymity is protected, nothing in the process impedes reporting to the SEC (Rule 21F-17), and reporters are shielded from retaliation (SOX 806, Dodd-Frank). Good looks like every case tracked to closure in one system, the Audit Committee seeing every accounting complaint plus quarterly metrics, and zero substantiated retaliation.
processes.owner: Ethics & Compliance (program owner), Legal (SOX/SEC matters), Audit Committee (oversight of accounting complaints)
processes.trigger: Report received through the hotline or web portal, or referred from ER-01 triage; quarterly Audit Committee reporting cycle
outputs: Case file with anonymity-preserving communication log
Audit Committee referral for accounting, internal-control and auditing complaints
Quarterly Audit Committee hotline report (volume, categories, aging, outcomes, retaliation claims)
Restricted protected-activity flag for named reporters
Annual hotline program effectiveness review
processes.sla: SOX-category complaints to the Audit Committee chair within 5 business days; reporter updates every 30 days; case closure target 60 days

steps.label: Report via hotline or portal
steps.detail: Reporter uses the third-party hotline (phone or web, in English, Mandarin, Hindi and Kannada) with an anonymous option and a report key for two-way messaging.

steps.label: Log & classify case
steps.detail: Log the case and tag categories: accounting/auditing/internal controls (SOX 301), securities fraud, bribery, export/sanctions, HR conduct. Restrict any reporter identity to the named case team.
steps.control: Reporter identity visible only to named case team; access log reviewed quarterly

steps.label: Accounting, audit or securities?
steps.detail: Legal decides whether the report concerns questionable accounting, internal accounting controls, auditing or securities law, which must follow the Audit Committee's procedures.

steps.label: Audit Committee oversight
steps.detail: The Audit Committee chair is notified, and the committee directs or approves the investigation plan and may retain independent counsel or forensic accountants. Legal decides whether the external auditor must be informed.
steps.control: Every SOX-category complaint reported to the Audit Committee chair

steps.label: Investigate & update reporter
steps.detail: The assigned owner investigates using the ER-02 method; E&C updates the reporter through the portal at least every 30 days without disclosing confidential details and never asks anonymous reporters to identify themselves.

steps.label: Protect named reporters
steps.detail: Named reporters get a restricted protected-activity flag in Darwinbox; any proposed adverse action against them for 12 months needs ER and Legal review (SOX 806, Dodd-Frank, CA 90-day presumption).
steps.control: Adverse action against flagged reporters requires Legal sign-off

steps.label: Findings, remediation & disclosure
steps.detail: Legal reviews findings and remediation (control fixes, discipline via ER-04, restatement analysis) and decides on self-disclosure to DOJ/SEC, SOX 302 sub-certification updates or 8-K implications.

steps.label: Close & report quarterly
steps.detail: Close the case with outcome and root cause. The quarterly Audit Committee report covers reports per 100 employees, category mix, substantiation rate, aging, retaliation claims and remediation status.

steps.label: Audit Committee reviews program
steps.detail: The Audit Committee reviews the quarterly report and the annual effectiveness review (awareness survey results, benchmark comparison, hotline vendor performance).

controls.control: All SOX-category complaints escalated to the Audit Committee chair within 5 business days
controls.evidence: Escalation log and Audit Committee minutes

controls.control: Annual Rule 21F-17 scan of codes, NDAs, PIIAs, separation agreements and interview scripts for language impeding regulator contact
Quarterly review of who accessed reporter identities

kpis.name: SOX-category complaints escalated on time
kpis.why: Audit Committee oversight is a listing and SOX 301 requirement

kpis.name: Median days to close
kpis.why: Slow handling pushes reporters to regulators and forfeits self-disclosure credit

kpis.name: Substantiated retaliation claims
kpis.why: Retaliation liability often exceeds the underlying issue

kpis.name: Reports per 100 employees
kpis.why: Tracks awareness and trust in the channel

considerations: Never require internal reporting first or notice to the company before contacting a regulator; the SEC treats the language itself as a Rule 21F-17 violation even if never enforced.
SOX 806 protects internal reports, while Dodd-Frank anti-retaliation remedies require a report to the SEC (Digital Realty); SOX claims cannot be forced into arbitration.
Speed matters: DOJ's corporate whistleblower program lets a company keep declination eligibility only if it self-reports within 120 days of an internal report.
Screen the hotline vendor and its sub-processors: staff in China with access to bulk US employee data can make the contract a restricted transaction under the DOJ Data Security Program.

variations.when: Report implicates the CEO, CFO or an Audit Committee member
variations.how: Hotline vendor routes directly to the Audit Committee chair (or Board chair) and excludes implicated individuals from case access; independent counsel investigates.

variations.when: Reporter has already contacted the SEC or another agency
variations.how: Legal-only handling, no questions about the agency contact, preservation hold, and heightened retaliation monitoring.

variations.when: Report concerns export control or sanctions
variations.how: Trade Compliance and Legal lead, assessing voluntary self-disclosure to BIS or OFAC and immediate containment of further releases.

countries.us: SOX 301 (Rule 10A-3) requires Audit Committee procedures for confidential, anonymous complaints on accounting and auditing; SOX 806 claims go to OSHA within 180 days, and Dodd-Frank adds double back pay for SEC reporters. Rule 21F-17 enforcement continues (Foot Locker, May 2026), so no policy or agreement may require notice to the company before contacting regulators.
countries.us-ca: LC 1102.5 protects reports to government agencies and to internal supervisors, the Labor Commissioner whistleblower hotline notice must be posted (LC 1102.8), and adverse action within 90 days is presumed retaliatory (SB 497), with penalties up to $10,000 per violation.
countries.ca: Criminal Code s.425.1 makes retaliation against employees who report offences to authorities a crime, and ESA, OHSA and BC pay-transparency complaints carry their own anti-reprisal rules. Give BC employees notice of hotline purposes under PIPA.
countries.in: The Companies Act s.177 vigil mechanism is mandatory for listed or large-borrowing companies and expected otherwise, so adopt the global hotline as the Indian subsidiary's vigil mechanism with Board-level oversight. Hotline data is governed by the SPDI Rules until DPDP duties start on 13 May 2027.
countries.tw: No general private-sector whistleblower protection statute is in force (verify), so protection rests on the company program plus GEEA and OSH Act anti-retaliation rules for harassment and bullying reports. Disclose hotline processing and transfer to the US vendor in the PDPA notice.
countries.cn: Anonymous reporting is lawful, but a US-hosted hotline is a cross-border transfer requiring PIPL notice, a transfer basis and a PIPIA. Have counsel review how export-control or sanctions findings are framed, given the Anti-Foreign Sanctions Law.

processes.name: Conflict-of-interest disclosure
processes.summary: Annual and event-driven disclosure of outside employment, board and advisory seats, investments in suppliers, customers or competitors, relatives in the reporting line or at counterparties, foreign talent programs and side businesses, which are common among engineers in China and Taiwan. Good looks like 100% certification of the in-scope population, every disclosed conflict cleared, mitigated or prohibited within 15 business days, and related-person items fed to the proxy.
processes.owner: Ethics & Compliance (program), Legal (executive & related-person items), Manager (mitigation)
processes.trigger: Annual certification cycle; hire (TA-10); promotion into a decision-making role; any new outside activity, investment, board seat or relationship
outputs: Annual COI certification records
Disclosure decision (cleared, mitigated, prohibited) with conditions
Signed mitigation plan (recusal, reassignment, divestment)
Related-person transaction log for the proxy (Item 404)
Outside-activity pre-approval register
processes.sla: Annual certification within 30 days of launch; each disclosure decided within 15 business days

steps.label: Disclose on annual or event trigger
steps.detail: Employee completes the COI questionnaire annually with the Code attestation, at hire and within 30 days of a change: outside work and advisory roles, board seats, material holdings in suppliers, customers or competitors, relatives at the company or counterparties, foreign talent programs, and side businesses.

steps.label: Screen & auto-clear
steps.detail: 'No' answers auto-clear; any 'yes' routes to review. E&C cross-checks disclosed entities against the vendor master and customer lists and flags semiconductor, EDA, IP or design-service companies.

steps.label: Conflict type?
steps.detail: Classify as no conflict, manageable, or executive/related-person (directors, executive officers and their immediate family), which goes to Legal.

steps.label: Agree mitigation conditions
steps.detail: Manager and E&C set conditions: recusal from vendor selection, no use of company time, EDA tools or IP, a divestment timeline, or a reporting-line change for relatives. The employee signs the conditions.

steps.label: Review executive & related items
steps.detail: Legal assesses whether the item is a Code waiver (Nasdaq 5610: board approval and disclosure within 4 business days) or an Item 404 related-person transaction over $120,000, and routes it to the Audit Committee.

steps.label: Apply HR changes & record
steps.detail: HRBP implements reporting-line changes under POL-07, updates the outside-activity register, and flags outside work in semiconductor or AI that needs pre-approval.

steps.label: Monitor conditions & escalate
steps.detail: Check open mitigation plans quarterly; escalate red flags (founding a competing start-up, talent-plan applications, undisclosed supplier interests) to Legal and Security, and send breaches to ER-02.
steps.control: Quarterly monitoring of open mitigation plans

steps.label: Certification archived
steps.detail: Certifications and decisions are archived; completion is reported to the Audit Committee with non-responders escalated to Dept Heads.

controls.control: Certification completion tracked with escalation of non-responders at 30 and 45 days
Disclosed entities matched against vendor master and customer list
Related-person transactions pre-approved by the Audit Committee

kpis.name: Certification completion
kpis.why: Required evidence for the Code program and proxy disclosures

kpis.name: Disclosure decision cycle time
kpis.why: Slow reviews push employees to stop disclosing

kpis.name: Undisclosed conflicts found in investigations
kpis.why: Measures whether the disclosure program is trusted and understood

considerations: California bars discipline for lawful off-duty conduct, so rules must target use of company time, tools or IP and direct competition rather than banning moonlighting outright.
Undisclosed talent-plan participation, side ventures and advisory roles recur in chip and AI trade-secret cases; ask about them explicitly and apply the rules regardless of national origin.
Collect the minimum financial detail needed (entity, role, approximate stake band); financial data is sensitive under India's SPDI Rules and PIPL.
Relatives of government officials or state-owned customer staff are an FCPA issue as well as a COI; route them to Compliance.

variations.when: Executive officer or director
variations.how: Legal and the Audit Committee decide; a waiver requires board approval and disclosure within four business days (Form 8-K Item 5.05 or website).

variations.when: Employee wants an external board or start-up advisory role
variations.how: Pre-approval with no competitive overlap, a time limit, and insider-trading review of any equity received.

variations.when: China employee holds a stake in a supplier or customer
variations.how: E&C review with China counsel; unresolved harmful concurrent roles can support Art. 39 dismissal only if the handbook defines them.

countries.us: Nasdaq Rule 5610 requires a public code with disclosed executive waivers, and Item 404 requires disclosure of related-person transactions over $120,000, including employed relatives of directors and officers. Staff on federally funded R&D may need malign foreign talent program certifications (CHIPS Act s10632; verify applicability).
countries.us-ca: Lawful off-duty conduct and political activity are protected (LC 96(k), 98.6, 1101-1102), so COI rules must be tied to company time, tools, IP and competition; LC 2870 limits invention claims to inventions related to the business.
countries.ca: No COI statute, but Ontario's non-compete ban makes in-term COI and fiduciary duties for senior technical leaders more important. Competition Act s.45 criminalizes wage-fixing and no-poach agreements, so relationships with competitor HR staff are relevant disclosures.
countries.in: In-term exclusivity and anti-moonlighting clauses are enforceable (Contract Act s.27 bars only post-employment restraints), so require disclosure of outside work, directorships and start-up investments. Collect financial details with consent under the SPDI Rules until DPDP applies.
countries.tw: Side businesses and family-company roles are common; require disclosure and pre-approval, and treat undisclosed PRC-linked roles or investments as a national-security red flag given MJIB talent-poaching enforcement. Capture government-funded core key technology project roles, which carry travel-approval duties.
countries.cn: Concurrent employment that seriously affects work, or continues after the employer objects, is an Art. 39 dismissal ground only if handbook rules define it. Anti-Unfair Competition Law commercial-bribery rules make undisclosed relationships with customer staff a serious-violation risk.

processes.name: Threat assessment & workplace violence
processes.summary: Handles threats, violent incidents and concerning behavior (including online threats and domestic violence reaching the workplace) through a multidisciplinary Threat Assessment Team, from emergency response to risk assessment, protective measures and statutory records such as California's WVPP violent incident log. Good looks like emergency services called within minutes for imminent danger, the team convened within 4 hours for credible threats, and every incident logged and fed into hazard correction.
processes.owner: Security (Threat Assessment Team lead), Employee Relations (people actions), EHS (WVPP / OHSA program compliance), Legal
processes.trigger: Report of violence, a threat, intimidation, stalking, domestic violence affecting the workplace, or concerning behavior in person or online
outputs: Violent incident log entry (CA WVPP) or site incident report
Threat assessment record with risk level and management plan
Protective measures (access suspension, escorts, restraining order petition)
Post-incident investigation and hazard corrections
Support referrals (EAP) for affected employees
processes.sla: Imminent danger: emergency services immediately; credible threat: Threat Assessment Team within 4 hours; incident logged within 1 business day (internal standard)

steps.label: Threat or incident reported
steps.detail: Anyone reports through the Security line, a manager, ER-01 channels or, for imminent danger, emergency services first. Online threats and domestic violence risks are in scope.

steps.label: Imminent danger?
steps.detail: Security duty officer assesses within minutes whether anyone is in immediate danger.

steps.label: Emergency response & lockdown
steps.detail: Call police, run the site emergency plan (shelter or evacuate), suspend the person's badge access and notify leadership. In California, employees may leave a workplace they reasonably believe is unsafe during an emergency (LC 1139).

steps.label: Convene Threat Assessment Team
steps.detail: Security lead, ER, Legal, EHS, HRBP and an EAP adviser (plus an external threat assessor for high-risk cases) gather facts, history, access, online activity and stressors, and rate risk with a structured professional-judgment tool.

steps.label: Protective & interim people actions
steps.detail: Paid administrative leave for the person of concern, badge and VPN suspension via ITSM, no-contact directives, and schedule or remote-work changes for targets. Base actions on behavior, never on a diagnosis.
steps.control: Access suspension executed within 1 hour of the team's decision

steps.label: Restraining order & police liaison
steps.detail: Legal decides on workplace violence restraining orders (CA CCP 527.8, available for harassment since 2025) or local equivalents, law-enforcement referral and notifications to targets.

steps.label: Log incident & correct hazards
steps.detail: Record the incident in the WVPP violent incident log (CA), OHSA program records (Ontario) or Taiwan prevention-plan records; run the post-incident investigation and assign hazard corrections (access control, lighting, visitor rules).
steps.control: Every incident logged; WVPP reviewed annually

steps.label: Support team & report recurrence
steps.detail: Manager briefs affected staff on a need-to-know basis with EAP support and reports any recurrence; return-to-work or separation of the person of concern follows ER-02/ER-04 or OF-02.

steps.label: Reassess & close
steps.detail: The team reassesses risk at 30 and 90 days and closes the case when risk is low and hazard corrections are complete; California WVPP records are kept 5 years.

raci.activity: WVPP / OHSA program, incident log & training

controls.control: Violent incident log maintained per site with required fields, and annual WVPP effectiveness review
controls.evidence: Incident log and annual review record

controls.control: Badge and system access suspended within 1 hour of a Threat Assessment Team decision
Annual interactive WVPP training (CA) and annual review of Ontario violence policy and program

kpis.name: Time to convene team for credible threats
kpis.why: Early structured assessment is what prevents escalation

kpis.name: Incidents logged within 1 business day
kpis.why: The CA incident log and post-incident investigation are statutory

kpis.name: Hazard corrections closed within 30 days
kpis.why: Shows the program learns from incidents

considerations: Assess behavior, not diagnosis: ADA and FEHA require an individualized 'direct threat' assessment, and mental-health information stays in confidential medical files.
Link the team to insider-risk monitoring: a disgruntled engineer with design-data access can be both a safety and a trade-secret risk (ER-10).
Domestic violence is a workplace issue: Ontario OHSA covers it where a worker may be harmed at work, and California victims are entitled to leave and safety accommodations (Gov Code 12945.8).
HR should never assess threats alone; use a trained, cross-functional team and a structured tool, and document why each measure was chosen.

variations.when: Threat from a non-employee (former employee, ex-partner, customer)
variations.how: Security and Facilities issue a visitor ban with photo at reception, Legal considers a restraining order, and the targeted employee gets a safety plan and victim-leave options.

variations.when: Threat of self-harm
variations.how: Treat as a crisis-support matter (EAP, emergency services if imminent) under medical confidentiality, not as discipline.

variations.when: Incident at an Asia site
variations.how: Local police and country HR lead; Taiwan unlawful-infringement prevention-plan records, and China handbook-based discipline for threats or violence.

countries.us: No federal workplace-violence standard exists, but the OSHA General Duty Clause applies and several states have their own rules. Responses involving mental health must follow the ADA individualized direct-threat analysis.
countries.us-ca: SB 553 (LC 6401.9) requires a site-specific WVPP developed with employee input, annual interactive training, a violent incident log, post-incident investigation, and 5-year records with employee access within 15 days; Cal/OSHA must adopt a general-industry standard by 31 Dec 2026. Employers may seek workplace violence restraining orders (CCP 527.8), including for harassment since 2025.
countries.ca: Ontario OHSA ss.32.0.1-32.0.5 require a written violence policy posted at 6+ workers, an annually reviewed program, a risk assessment and procedures to summon help, including for domestic violence, plus a duty to share information about a person with a history of violence where workers may encounter them (verify scope). BC requires a violence risk assessment and procedures under the OHS Regulation (ss.4.27-4.31; verify).
countries.in: No specific workplace-violence statute; rely on the OSH Code general duty, night-shift security and transport measures, and POSH where the conduct is sexual. Report criminal threats to police.
countries.tw: OSH Act Art. 6(2) requires measures to prevent unlawful infringement (physical or verbal violence), with a written plan and implementation records at sites of 100+ workers. The bullying chapter (1 July 2026) overlaps where coworkers are involved.
countries.cn: No dedicated statute; the Work Safety Law responsibility system applies, and threats or violence must be listed as serious violations in the democratically adopted handbook to support Art. 39 dismissal. Report criminal conduct to the public security bureau.

processes.name: Labor relations & employee consultation
processes.summary: Manages collective and consultative obligations: NLRA-compliant practices in the US, China's union and democratic procedure, Taiwan's quarterly labor-management meetings, India's grievance committee, works committee and standing orders, and Canada's safety committees and organizing readiness. Good looks like statutory bodies that never lapse, consultation completed before changes take effect, and no unfair-labor-practice or labor-bureau exposure.
processes.owner: Employee Relations (global labor relations), country HR leads (local bodies), Legal (labor counsel)
processes.trigger: Planned change affecting terms, rules or vital interests (handbook, hours, pay structure, reorganization); statutory meeting calendar; union organizing activity or demand
outputs: Statutory body calendar and membership register (Taiwan LMM, India GRC, China union/employee congress, Canada JHSC)
Consultation record: materials, minutes, consents, signed acknowledgments
Authority filings (Taiwan LMM representative list and OT consents; India standing orders)
Manager guidance on NLRA-lawful communication
Labor-relations risk log
processes.sla: Consultation complete before the change's effective date; Taiwan meetings at least quarterly; India GRC grievances resolved within 30 days

steps.label: Change or LR event identified
steps.detail: HRBP flags a planned change (handbook, hours, bonus structure, reorganization, relocation) or labor-relations event (organizing, petition, collective grievance) to ER through the change intake form.

steps.label: Map duties by country
steps.detail: Map what applies: China democratic procedure for rules affecting vital interests (LCL Art. 4); Taiwan LMM consent for overtime and flexible hours; India standing-order and GRC steps; US bargaining for any unionized unit; Canada safety-committee input.

steps.label: Consultation or bargaining needed?
steps.detail: Legal confirms whether consultation, consent or bargaining is legally required, and the sequence and timing.

steps.label: Prepare consultation pack
steps.detail: Local-language materials covering rationale, proposed text, impact and timeline. In China, circulate to the employee congress or all employees for discussion before consulting the union or representatives.

steps.label: Consult, vote or bargain
steps.detail: Taiwan LMM (equal labor and management representatives) records consent; China union or representatives give opinions; India GRC or works committee considers; US unions bargain over mandatory subjects. Both sides sign the minutes.
steps.control: Signed minutes or consent record before implementation

steps.label: Finalize & file where required
steps.detail: Incorporate feedback, finalize text, and file where required (Taiwan work rules with the local authority; India standing orders; Taiwan overtime arrangements at 30+ employee sites).

steps.label: Communicate lawfully to teams
steps.detail: Managers use approved talking points; US managers avoid threats, interrogation, promises and surveillance, and keep meetings on union topics voluntary.

steps.label: Acknowledge rules / raise issues
steps.detail: Employees sign acknowledgment of new rules (the publicity evidence China requires) and can raise grievances through the India GRC (within 1 year) or ER channels.

steps.label: Evidence stored & calendar set
steps.detail: Consultation evidence is stored with the policy version (DS-08) and the statutory body calendar is updated for the next cycle.

raci.activity: Statutory bodies maintenance (LMM, GRC, JHSC, union)

controls.control: No rule or handbook change goes live in China, Taiwan or India without consultation evidence linked in the policy register
controls.evidence: DS-08 register entry with minutes and acknowledgments

controls.control: Quarterly check that statutory bodies met and are properly constituted (Taiwan LMM, India GRC, JHSC)
Annual review of US handbook rules against the current NLRB standard (Stericycle)

kpis.name: Statutory meetings held on schedule
kpis.why: A missed Taiwan LMM invalidates overtime consent

kpis.name: Changes implemented with complete consultation evidence
kpis.why: Unconsulted rules are unenforceable in China

kpis.name: Unfair labor practice charges or labor-bureau complaints
kpis.why: Direct measure of labor-relations risk

considerations: China's democratic procedure is evidence-driven: keep circulation records, feedback received and responses, or the handbook will not support dismissals.
Taiwan labor-management meetings must actually meet every quarter with elected representatives; paper-only meetings leave overtime and flexible-hour arrangements without valid consent.
The NLRA protects concerted activity by non-union employees too; policy wording, social-media rules and investigation instructions all need Section 7 review.
India's 'worker' definition catches many individual-contributor engineers, so GRC and standing-order thresholds are often met sooner than HQ expects; the Karnataka IT union (KITU) is active.
BC's single-step card-check means a campaign can certify quickly; prepare managers on lawful communication before it is needed.

variations.when: Union organizing campaign (US or Canada)
variations.how: Legal-led response, manager training on lawful conduct, voluntary-only meetings on union topics, and no changes to terms during the campaign without Legal review.

variations.when: Mass layoff
variations.how: China: 30-day explanation to the union or all staff and a labor-bureau report (Shanghai 2026 rules); Taiwan: Mass Redundancy Act 60-day plan and negotiation; executed through OF-03.

variations.when: Change reduces entitlements (e.g., Shanghai sick pay after the August 2026 lapse)
variations.how: Full democratic procedure, a reasonableness and grandfathering analysis, and Legal sign-off before announcement.

countries.us: NLRA Section 7 protects concerted activity by non-supervisory employees with or without a union; Stericycle, McLaren Macomb and Cemex remain binding although GC 26-04 targets them. Unionized units require bargaining over mandatory subjects before changes.
countries.us-ca: SB 399's captive-audience ban (LC 1137) is preliminarily enjoined with a Ninth Circuit decision pending, but keep union-topic meetings voluntary; AB 288's PERB backstop is largely enjoined as NLRA-preempted.
countries.ca: No works councils or mandatory consultation outside unionized workplaces; joint health and safety committees are required at 20+ workers in Ontario and BC. BC's single-step card-check can certify a union quickly.
countries.in: A GRC is required at 20+ workers (grievances resolved within 30 days), a works committee at 100+ when directed, and standing orders at 300+ workers. The Karnataka IT standing-orders exemption (to June 2029) is conditional on a GRC and POSH IC, and its status under the IR Code needs confirmation.
countries.tw: Labor-management meetings are mandatory for all employers at least quarterly with equal representatives, and their consent is required for overtime, flexible hours and shift-rest changes where there is no union. Enterprise unions may form with 30+ members.
countries.cn: Rules affecting vital interests must go through democratic procedure and be publicized (LCL Art. 4); union funds of 2% of payroll are payable (commonly collected by the tax bureau). The union must be notified before any unilateral termination (LCL Art. 43).

processes.name: Legal hold & litigation support
processes.summary: Preserves HR records and employee data once litigation, agency charges, audits or government investigations are reasonably anticipated, and supports discovery and agency responses. Good looks like hold notices within 2 business days of the trigger, departing custodians' data preserved before deprovisioning, holds that override retention purges, and documented releases.
processes.owner: Legal (hold owner), People Ops (HR record custodian), IT (system preservation)
processes.trigger: Demand letter, agency charge (EEOC, CRD, HRTO, labor arbitration), lawsuit, subpoena, regulator inquiry, an investigation likely to lead to claims, or a RIF with anticipated claims
outputs: Legal hold notice and custodian list
Custodian acknowledgments
System preservation confirmations (mail, chat, Darwinbox, Greenhouse, payroll)
Hold flags suppressing deletion in HR systems
Collection and production log
Hold release notice
processes.sla: Hold notice within 2 business days of trigger; system preservation within 1 business day of notice; acknowledgments within 5 business days

steps.label: Trigger event identified
steps.detail: Legal receives a demand letter, charge, lawsuit or subpoena, or ER escalates a matter where litigation is reasonably anticipated, and opens a hold matter.

steps.label: Identify custodians & sources
steps.detail: ER and the HRBP list custodians (decision-makers, managers, HR, witnesses) and sources: Darwinbox records, Greenhouse requisitions and scorecards, payroll, performance data, ER case files, email and chat, and personal devices used for work.

steps.label: Issue hold notice
steps.detail: Plain-language notice (Chinese for China and Taiwan custodians) with scope, date range and 'do not delete' instruction, covering WeChat, LINE and WhatsApp used for work. Custodians acknowledge by e-signature; reminders go out quarterly.
steps.control: Acknowledgments tracked; non-responders escalated at 5 bd

steps.label: Preserve systems & stop deletion
steps.detail: IT places in-place holds on mailboxes and chat and suspends auto-deletion; People Ops sets hold flags in Darwinbox and Greenhouse so DS-03 purge jobs skip held records.
steps.control: Hold flags override automated deletion jobs

steps.label: Custodian leaving?
steps.detail: Before any offboarding, People Ops checks resignations and terminations against the active-hold custodian list.

steps.label: Preserve leaver data first
steps.detail: Before OF-06 access removal and device wipe, IT images the laptop and phone and preserves mailbox and drives; the device cannot be reissued until Legal clears it.

steps.label: Support collection & facts
steps.detail: Managers and HR provide documents and context for pleadings and agency responses (EEOC position statements, arbitration evidence); IT or an eDiscovery vendor collects, never the custodian.

steps.label: Apply cross-border & privacy limits
steps.detail: For China data, obtain approval before providing it to foreign courts or enforcement bodies (PIPL Art. 41, Data Security Law Art. 36); minimize and redact third-party personal data and use protective orders.

steps.label: Release hold
steps.detail: After final resolution and appeal periods, Legal issues a written release and records return to the DS-03 retention schedule.

controls.control: Offboarding workflow checks the active-hold custodian list before any device wipe or account deletion
Quarterly reconciliation of system hold flags to active matters
Exception report of records deleted by purge jobs despite a hold flag

kpis.name: Hold notices issued within 2 business days
kpis.why: The duty to preserve starts at reasonable anticipation, not service

kpis.name: Custodian acknowledgments within 5 business days
kpis.why: Unacknowledged holds are hard to defend

kpis.name: Spoliation incidents
kpis.why: Lost evidence brings sanctions and adverse inferences

considerations: Internal investigations and RIFs are frequent hold triggers; ER should call Legal when a case looks likely to become a claim, not when a letter arrives.
Departing employees are the biggest gap: laptops wiped for reissue destroy the evidence most often needed.
Holds override privacy deletion rights; record the legal basis so DSAR responses (DS-02) can cite it.
China-resident data cannot simply be exported for US discovery; plan onshore review and approvals early.

variations.when: Agency charge (EEOC, CRD, HRTO)
variations.how: Preserve all relevant personnel records until final disposition (29 CFR 1602.14) and prepare the position statement with ER.

variations.when: Government investigation (SEC, DOJ, BIS)
variations.how: Outside counsel leads, holds are broader (including trade and export records), and nothing related is destroyed.

variations.when: China-resident custodians
variations.how: Data stays in China and is reviewed onshore through local counsel or a local vendor, with approvals before any transfer.

countries.us: The duty to preserve starts when litigation is reasonably anticipated, and failure to preserve ESI invites FRCP 37(e) sanctions. Once an EEOC charge is filed, keep all relevant personnel records until final disposition (29 CFR 1602.14).
countries.us-ca: CRD complaints can be filed within 3 years (Gov Code 12960) and wage and PAGA claims reach back years, so holds are frequent. CCPA deletion requests can be declined for records needed to establish or defend legal claims (verify exception wording).
countries.ca: Ontario's basic limitation period is 2 years (Limitations Act, 2002) and HRTO applications 1 year; keep harassment investigation files for the limitation period and any hold.
countries.in: Preserve for labor disputes and civil suits (Limitation Act 1963, generally 3 years). DPDP allows retention required by law, and CERT-In already requires ICT logs to be kept 180 days.
countries.tw: Under the Labor Incident Act employers must produce attendance and wage records in labor litigation, and missing records shift the burden of proof to the employer; wage claims generally run 5 years (Civil Code Art. 126).
countries.cn: Labor arbitration has a 1-year limitation period and employers bear the burden of proof for records they control. PIPL Art. 41 and Data Security Law Art. 36 prohibit providing data stored in China to foreign judicial or enforcement bodies without approval.

processes.name: Trade-secret protection for departing employees
processes.summary: Risk-tiered exit protocol for employees with access to chip designs, source code, roadmaps or customer data: DLP lookback, device imaging, return-and-deletion certification, reminder letters, and jurisdiction-specific tools (no non-competes in California; paid non-competes in China and Taiwan; garden leave in India). Good looks like high-risk exits identified the day notice is given, lookback completed before the last day, and remedies preserved through documented 'reasonable protective measures'.
processes.owner: Security / Insider Risk (lead), Legal (IP & employment), HRBP (process), IT (access & devices)
processes.trigger: Resignation or termination notice for an employee in a flagged role (design, verification, architecture, packaging, FAE, sales with roadmap access) or with a going-to-competitor indicator
outputs: Risk tier (1-3) with rationale
DLP and download lookback report (30-90 days)
Forensic device images for tier 1
Signed return-and-deletion certification
Post-employment obligations reminder letter
Non-compete activate or release decision and payment set-up (China, Taiwan)
processes.sla: Risk tier within 1 business day of notice; lookback before last day; certification on last day

steps.label: Departure notice logged
steps.detail: A resignation or termination in a flagged job family triggers ER-10 from Darwinbox; the HRBP asks (not demands) about the next employer and role and records the answer.

steps.label: Assign risk tier
steps.detail: Tier 1: crown-jewel design data or core key technology access, going to a competitor or PRC-linked entity, or anomalous activity. Tier 2: flagged role with benign destination. Tier 3: standard exit.

steps.label: Run DLP lookback review
steps.detail: Review 30-90 days of downloads, repository clones, cloud uploads, USB, printing and forwarding to personal email under the disclosed monitoring policy; escalate anomalies to Legal.
steps.control: Lookback documented for every tier 1-2 exit before the last day

steps.label: Anomalies or tier 1?
steps.detail: Legal decides on accelerated access cut-off, garden leave, device imaging, an exit interview with Legal present, and any TRO or law-enforcement referral.

steps.label: Restrict access & image devices
steps.detail: Immediately narrow access to sensitive repositories and EDA projects and image laptop and phone before return, preserving under ER-09.

steps.label: Update export & TCP records
steps.detail: Update deemed-export licence and technology control plan records for foreign-national leavers, and remind Taiwan staff on government-funded core key technology projects of continuing travel-approval duties.

steps.label: Exit meeting & certification
steps.detail: Review confidentiality, invention assignment and the DTSA immunity notice; collect devices and badges; obtain a signed return-and-deletion certification. Never withhold final pay for unreturned items (CA LC 221).
