steps.control: Signed certification retained for all tier 1-2 exits

steps.label: Non-compete decision & letter
steps.detail: Decide whether to activate or release any non-compete (China: monthly pay of at least 30% of prior 12-month average; Taiwan: at least 50%, max 2 years) and set up payments; send a reminder letter to the employee and, only where warranted, to the new employer.

steps.label: Confirm handover & credentials
steps.detail: Manager confirms knowledge transfer happened through company systems, no personal copies were kept, and shared credentials and service accounts were rotated.

steps.label: Monitoring window closed
steps.detail: Security watches for residual access attempts for 30 days, then closes the case with evidence retained under the schedule or any hold.

controls.control: Flagged-role terminations in Darwinbox automatically open an ER-10 case
Lookback review completed before the last day for tier 1-2 exits
Non-compete decision recorded at exit and payments set up in payroll where activated
Leaver's PIIA checked for the DTSA immunity notice and local IP clauses

kpis.name: Tier 1-2 lookbacks completed before last day
kpis.why: Evidence is easiest to secure while the employee is still on systems

kpis.name: Signed exit certifications (tier 1-2)
kpis.why: The certification is key evidence for injunctions and prosecutions

kpis.name: Non-compete compensation paid on time (China, Taiwan)
kpis.why: Late or missing payments void the restraint

considerations: Trade-secret status depends on reasonable protective measures, so the exit protocol is itself evidence; apply it consistently.
Base risk on role, access and destination, never nationality, to avoid discrimination claims.
Monitoring used in lookbacks must be disclosed in advance (PIPL notice, DPDP s.7(i), Taiwan PDPA, Ontario e-monitoring policy).
In California, do not send letters threatening void non-competes; B&P 16600.5 gives employees a private right of action.
Do not sign non-competes with every engineer in China or Taiwan; they are void for staff without trade-secret access and cost money when activated.

variations.when: Departure to a PRC-linked or Entity List company
variations.how: Tier 1 automatically; Legal and Trade Compliance assess National Security Act (Taiwan) and export-control exposure, and Legal considers law-enforcement referral.

variations.when: Anomalous download discovered
variations.how: Legal demands return and certification, conducts a forensic interview, and assesses a TRO under CUTSA/DTSA or local injunctions.

variations.when: India engineer on 60-90 day notice
variations.how: Use garden leave with restricted access; still issue the relieving letter and pay final dues within 2 working days of the last day.

countries.us: Every PIIA must include the DTSA immunity notice (18 U.S.C. 1833(b)) or exemplary damages and fees are lost against that individual. Non-competes are void in CA, MN, ND, OK and WY (WA from 30 Jun 2027), so rely on NDAs, invention assignment and narrow non-solicits.
countries.us-ca: B&P 16600/16600.5 void non-competes and most non-solicits and California rejects inevitable disclosure, so protection rests on CUTSA-ready controls: tiered access, DLP, exit certification, device imaging and prompt TRO action. Final pay cannot be withheld for unreturned property (LC 221).
countries.ca: Ontario bans employee non-competes below the C-suite (ESA s.67.2) and BC courts rarely enforce them, so use confidentiality, narrow 12-month non-solicits and working notice or garden leave. Criminal Code s.391 criminalizes obtaining trade secrets by deceit.
countries.in: Post-employment non-competes are void (Contract Act s.27), but garden leave on full pay during the notice period is enforceable. With no trade-secret statute, protection rests on contract, confidentiality injunctions and DPDP s.7(i)-based monitoring.
countries.tw: Non-competes are valid only under LSA Art. 9-1 (written, max 2 years, at least 50% of average monthly wage paid after exit). The National Security Act punishes misappropriation of national core key technologies (e.g., AI/HPC chip design, chiplet interconnect) with up to 12 years, and staff on government-funded core key technology projects need approval for mainland China travel even after leaving (Cross-Strait Act Art. 9).
countries.cn: Non-competes apply only to staff with real trade-secret access, max 2 years, with monthly compensation of at least 30% of prior 12-month average pay (generally 50% if longer than one year) under the MOHRSS 2025 Guidelines. Decide at exit whether to activate or release, since release mid-restriction costs 3 extra months of compensation.

processes.name: Employee data changes & data quality
processes.summary: Controls how employee master data (job, org, compensation, location, personal and bank details) is requested, approved, effective-dated and synchronized between Greenhouse, Darwinbox and the payroll providers, with monthly reconciliations and a data-quality scorecard. Good looks like 99.5%+ accuracy on payroll-critical fields, almost no retro pay caused by late changes, and every change traceable to an approved request.
processes.owner: People Ops (HRIS data steward), Payroll (payroll data), HR Analytics (data-quality reporting)
processes.trigger: Employee self-service update, manager or HRBP transaction request, Greenhouse-to-Darwinbox hire handoff, or a reconciliation exception
outputs: Approved, effective-dated transaction in Darwinbox
Payroll change feed and payroll confirmation
Monthly Darwinbox-Greenhouse-payroll reconciliation with exception log
Data-quality scorecard by country and field
Statutory change notices or written agreements where required
processes.sla: Changes entered at least 3 business days before payroll cut-off; reconciliation exceptions resolved within 5 business days

steps.label: Change requested
steps.detail: Employee updates personal data (address, bank, emergency contact, legal name) in Darwinbox self-service, or a manager or HRBP submits a job, pay, org or location change with effective date and reason code.

steps.label: Approve per matrix
steps.detail: Workflow routes by change type: pay changes follow the approval matrix (Total Rewards for out-of-range), location changes go to Payroll and Mobility for tax registration, and bank changes require re-authentication.

steps.label: Validate & effective-date
steps.detail: Data steward checks documents, effective date (no backdating beyond the open pay period without Payroll approval) and reason code, plus local rules: written agreement for pay, role or location changes in China, and the 50% 'wages' test in India.
steps.control: Maker-checker: the user who enters a change cannot approve it

steps.label: Pay impact after cut-off?
steps.detail: Decide whether the change affects pay and misses the current payroll cut-off.

steps.label: Plan retro or off-cycle
steps.detail: Payroll chooses retro in the next cycle or an off-cycle payment (PY-02), checking final-pay and statutory deadlines, and records the reason.

steps.label: Sync downstream systems
steps.detail: Integrations push the change to payroll, identity (Okta) and benefits. Greenhouse offer data is locked after the hire handoff so Darwinbox is the single source of truth.

steps.label: Confirm in pre-payroll review
steps.detail: Payroll confirms changes in the pre-payroll variance report and logs mismatches as exceptions.
steps.control: Pre-payroll variance review signed by the payroll lead

steps.label: Reconcile & publish scorecard
steps.detail: Monthly reconciliation of Darwinbox to payroll (headcount, base pay, cost center, bank) and Greenhouse offers to Darwinbox hires; publish a data-quality scorecard by country and field and route exceptions to owners.
steps.control: Monthly three-way reconciliation with exception sign-off

steps.label: Exceptions resolved
steps.detail: Exceptions are corrected with an audit trail and root causes (integration, training, process) feed quarterly improvements.

controls.control: Maker-checker segregation on all pay-impacting changes
Monthly Darwinbox-payroll-Greenhouse reconciliation with signed exceptions
Bank-detail changes require MFA re-authentication and a call-back for flagged risk

kpis.name: Payroll-critical field accuracy
kpis.why: Errors here become wage claims and SOX deficiencies

kpis.name: Retro transactions (changes after cut-off)
kpis.why: Retro pay drives wage-statement errors and off-cycle cost

kpis.name: Reconciliation exceptions older than 5 business days
kpis.why: Aged exceptions signal broken integrations

considerations: Declare one source of truth per data domain: Greenhouse until hire, Darwinbox after, and payroll only for calculated results.
Backdated pay changes create wage-statement problems in California and constructive-dismissal risk in Canada when they cut pay; enforce effective-dating discipline.
Payroll-diversion phishing targets bank-change requests; treat bank changes as high risk.
A work-location change can trigger a new US state registration or a new country entity; route it through MV-04 before the effective date.
Compensation changes are in SOX scope, so keep approval evidence and reports that can be relied on (IPE).

variations.when: Mass changes (merit cycle, reorganization)
variations.how: Bulk upload with pre- and post-load reconciliation and sample testing, coordinated with CO-02 or PL-04.

variations.when: Remote work state or country change
variations.how: Mobility, Payroll and Tax approve before the effective date via MV-04, including any new state or country registration.

variations.when: Legal name or gender-marker change
variations.how: Update discreetly with documents as local law requires and propagate to identity, benefits and payroll.

countries.us: A work-state change triggers state payroll registration, withholding and notice obligations. Keep I-9 data in a separate system or file, not in general HRIS records.
countries.us-ca: Non-exempt employees must get written notice of changes to their LC 2810.5 wage notice information within 7 calendar days (verify), inaccurate wage statements carry LC 226 penalties, and job title and wage history must be kept for employment plus 3 years (LC 432.3).
countries.ca: Ontario ESA requires employee and wage records for 3 years, and unilateral changes to pay, role or location risk constructive dismissal, so changes need consent or working notice.
countries.in: Keep the Codes' unified electronic registers current and make sure wage-structure changes keep 'wages' at 50% of remuneration, since PF, gratuity and leave encashment depend on it.
countries.tw: The employee roster (LSA Art. 7), wage and attendance records must be kept 5 years, and transfers must meet the five Art. 10-1 principles, including no reduction in wages or terms.
countries.cn: Changes to role, location or pay need written agreement (LCL Art. 35) reflected in the labor contract; Shanghai social insurance bases reset each July (RMB 7,546-37,731 from 1 Jul 2026).

processes.name: HR data subject requests
processes.summary: Handles requests from employees, former employees, candidates and contractors to access, correct, delete or restrict their personal data, plus statutory personnel-file and payroll-record requests, across six jurisdictions with different clocks. Good looks like every request logged, identity verified, deadlines tracked to the strictest applicable law, and responses complete while protecting third-party, privileged and held information.
processes.owner: People Ops (HR privacy desk), Legal / Privacy (exemptions & review)
processes.trigger: Request received through the privacy portal, email, HRBP or letter from an employee, former employee, candidate, contractor, authorized agent or attorney
outputs: Request log with jurisdiction, type and statutory deadline
Identity or agent verification record
Search results across HR systems
Response package (copies, corrections, deletion confirmation or reasoned refusal)
Extension notices where allowed
processes.sla: Strictest applicable clock: CA payroll records 21 days, CA personnel file 30 days, CCPA 45 days (+45), India DPDP 90 days from May 2027

steps.label: Request submitted
steps.detail: Requester submits through the privacy portal, email or an HRBP; anyone in HR who receives a request forwards it to the privacy desk within 1 business day.

steps.label: Log, classify & start clock
steps.detail: Log requester type, jurisdiction and request type (know/access, correct, delete, limit, personnel file, payroll records) and compute the deadline from the strictest applicable law.
steps.control: Deadline computed and tracked for every request

steps.label: Verify identity or agent
steps.detail: Verify identity in proportion to sensitivity (SSO for current staff; matched data points and confirmation for former staff and candidates) and verify any agent's or attorney's authority.

steps.label: Search HR systems
steps.detail: Search Darwinbox, Greenhouse, benefits, LMS, the ER case system and HR custodians' mail using the data map, and export records.

steps.label: Provide payroll records
steps.detail: Payroll pulls wage statements and payroll records (California: within 21 days) and confirms accuracy.

steps.label: Exemption or hold applies?
steps.detail: Legal checks for litigation holds, privilege, third-party personal data (e.g., witness statements), investigation confidentiality, retention obligations and trade secrets.

steps.label: Redact & document refusals
steps.detail: Redact third-party and privileged content and record the legal basis for each withheld category, including the requester's complaint or appeal rights.

steps.label: Respond securely
steps.detail: Deliver through the secure portal; for deletion, confirm what was deleted or de-identified and what was retained and why.

steps.label: Close & report metrics
steps.detail: Close the request and report volumes, types and timeliness to Privacy each quarter.

controls.control: Deadline tracker escalates at 50% and 80% of the statutory period
Legal review of every partial refusal or redaction
controls.evidence: Review record in the case file

controls.control: Identity verified before any disclosure

kpis.name: Responses on time
kpis.why: California personnel-file and payroll-record failures each carry $750 penalties

kpis.name: Median days to respond
kpis.why: Leaves margin under the shortest clocks

kpis.name: Regulator complaints arising from requests
kpis.why: Measures quality as well as speed

considerations: Employees often use access requests as pre-litigation discovery; coordinate with Legal, but the statutory clock keeps running.
Protect witnesses: investigation files can usually be withheld or redacted to the extent they reveal third-party information.
Deletion requests are answered by the retention schedule (DS-03); cite the retention basis rather than refusing generically.
One data map for all jurisdictions keeps searches proportionate; email and chat searches should be scoped by custodian and date.
Ontario employees have no statutory privacy access right against a provincially regulated employer, but responding as a matter of policy avoids inconsistency.

variations.when: Former employee in dispute or litigation
variations.how: Legal handles the request, coordinates with discovery, and avoids substantive discussion of the claims.

variations.when: Rejected candidate
variations.how: Search Greenhouse only; delete unless retention is required (California 4 years; Ontario applications 3 years).

variations.when: Request covers DLP or monitoring data
variations.how: Security joins the review; disclose categories and apply security exceptions where lawful.

countries.us: Outside California, employee privacy rights are limited, but many states give personnel-file inspection rights with deadlines (e.g., IL, MN, WA, OR, MA, MI, CT); route them through the same desk.
countries.us-ca: CCPA rights to know, delete, correct and limit apply to employees, applicants and contractors, with responses within 45 days (extendable by 45). Personnel files are due within 30 days (LC 1198.5, now including training records under SB 513) and payroll records within 21 days (LC 226), each with $750 penalties.
countries.ca: PIPEDA does not cover Ontario employees of a provincially regulated employer, but BC PIPA gives employees access rights handled by a designated privacy officer within about 30 business days (verify). Quebec Law 25 applies to any Quebec remote employee (verify timeline).
countries.in: From 13 May 2027 the DPDP Act gives rights of access, correction, erasure and grievance redressal, answered within 90 days; until then the SPDI Rules require a grievance officer.
countries.tw: The PDPA gives rights to inquire, review, obtain copies, correct, stop processing and delete; access requests are generally due within 15 days and correction or deletion within 30, each extendable once (verify).
countries.cn: PIPL Arts. 44-47 give rights to access, copy, correct, delete and port, and processors must offer a convenient request mechanism and give reasons for refusals (Art. 50). PIPL sets no fixed deadline, so target 15 working days (verify).

processes.name: Records retention & destruction
processes.summary: Maintains the HR retention schedule by record class and country, configures it in Darwinbox, Greenhouse, payroll, benefits, ER case and document systems, and runs defensible, logged destruction that always respects legal holds. Good looks like one cited schedule mapped to systems, automated purges with hold overrides, and annual destruction certificates.
processes.owner: People Ops (schedule owner), Legal (legal review & holds), IT (system purges)
processes.trigger: Annual schedule review; quarterly purge cycle; onboarding of a new HR system or vendor; a change in law
outputs: HR retention schedule by record class and country with citations
Retention rules configured per system
Quarterly purge-candidate report with hold check
Destruction logs and certificates (including vendors)
Retention periods per category for the CCPA notice
processes.sla: Schedule reviewed annually; purges quarterly; destruction logged within 5 business days

steps.label: Annual review triggered
steps.detail: Each Q1 People Ops reviews the schedule against research updates (e.g., CA SB 513, India's Code registers, Taiwan PDPA amendments) and new systems.

steps.label: Validate periods & citations
steps.detail: Set each period as the longest of statutory minimum, limitation period and business need (e.g., CA ADS data 4 years; Taiwan roster 5 years after departure; China terminated contracts 2 years; CRA payroll 6 years).

steps.label: Configure retention rules
steps.detail: Configure purge or de-identification rules in Darwinbox, Greenhouse (candidate data), the case system and document management.

steps.label: Confirm vendor deletion terms
steps.detail: Payroll, benefits, hotline and background-check vendors confirm retention settings and provide deletion certificates under their DPAs.

steps.label: Generate purge-candidate report
steps.detail: Quarterly report lists records past retention by system and country.

steps.label: On hold or in dispute?
steps.detail: Legal checks candidates against active holds (ER-09), open ER cases, agency charges and pending access requests.

steps.label: Exclude held records
steps.detail: Held records are excluded and tagged with the matter ID for re-evaluation at release.

steps.label: Confirm payroll & tax archives
steps.detail: Payroll confirms payroll and tax archives meet tax retention (US 4 years, Canada 6 years, China accounting vouchers 30 years) before any payroll-provider purge.

steps.label: Execute purge & log
steps.detail: Delete or irreversibly de-identify, logging record counts, systems, date and approver.
steps.control: Destruction log with approver and hold check

steps.label: File destruction certificate
steps.detail: Destruction certificate is filed and a summary goes to the privacy committee.

controls.control: Every purge batch passes a hold check signed by Legal
Destruction logged per system and vendor
Annual schedule approval with legal citations per record class

kpis.name: Records past retention not purged
kpis.why: Over-retention creates breach and discovery exposure and breaks CCPA, PIPL and DPDP limits

kpis.name: Purges executed with a documented hold check
kpis.why: Destroying held records is spoliation

kpis.name: Vendor deletion certificates received
kpis.why: Vendors often hold the largest HR data sets

considerations: Over-retention is a liability: the CCPA notice must state retention per category, and PIPL and DPDP require deletion once the purpose is served.
Decide per record class whether to apply the longest period globally or per country; per-country is more defensible for privacy but harder to run.
Keep medical, I-9 and demographic data in separate stores with their own periods (CA SB 464 requires demographic data to be kept apart).
Document how deleted data ages out of backups so deletion confirmations are accurate.

variations.when: New HR system or vendor
variations.how: Retention rules are configured and tested before go-live as a DS-06 condition.

variations.when: Acquired company records
variations.how: Map acquired records to the schedule, carry over existing holds, and purge legacy systems only after Legal review.

variations.when: Deceased or long-term-disabled employee
variations.how: Benefits, pension and insurance records are kept longer per plan and statutory terms.

countries.us: I-9s: the later of 3 years after hire or 1 year after termination; FLSA payroll 3 years (timecards 2); Title VII personnel records 1 year, or until final disposition once a charge is filed; OSHA 300 logs 5 years; exposure and medical records employment plus 30 years; ERISA 6 years.
countries.us-ca: Personnel files 3 years after termination; applications, personnel and ADS data 4 years (Gov Code 12946); payroll 3 years (4 recommended); job title and wage history employment plus 3 years; WVPP records 5 years; and the CCPA notice must state a period per category.
countries.ca: CRA payroll and tax records 6 years; Ontario ESA employee and wage records 3 years; Ontario postings, applications and interview-outcome records 3 years; ON disconnecting and e-monitoring policies 3 years after they cease to apply; BC ESA payroll 4 years after employment ends (verify).
countries.in: Keep unified electronic registers for the state-prescribed period (typically 3+ years; verify under final Karnataka rules) and tax records 6+ years. From May 2027 DPDP requires erasure once the purpose ends, while processing logs are kept at least 1 year.
countries.tw: Employee roster 5 years after departure, wage and attendance records 5 years, health exam records at least 7 years; delete or anonymize candidate and former-employee data once retention and litigation windows lapse (PDPA Art. 11).
countries.cn: Terminated labor contracts and termination records at least 2 years, wage records 2+ years, PIPIA reports 3 years, accounting vouchers 30 years; otherwise delete or anonymize when the purpose ends (PIPL Arts. 19, 47).

processes.name: HRIS access & segregation of duties
processes.summary: Governs who can see and change what in Darwinbox, Greenhouse, payroll and the equity platform as a SOX IT general control: role design, joiner-mover-leaver provisioning, quarterly user access reviews, privileged-access monitoring, and segregation between HR data entry and payroll approval. Good looks like no user able to create a worker, change pay and approve payroll, UARs done on time with nothing left unremediated, and no auditor findings.
processes.owner: People Ops (HRIS role owner), IT (identity & access), Payroll (payroll-system roles), Finance / Internal Audit (SOX testing)
processes.trigger: Access request, role change or termination; quarterly UAR cycle; new role design, system release or implementation partner access
outputs: Role catalog with SoD conflict matrix
Approved access tickets
Quarterly UAR sign-offs with removal evidence
Privileged-access and configuration-change log reviews
SOX control narratives and test evidence
processes.sla: Access provisioned within 2 business days of approval; leaver access removed same day; UAR completed within 15 business days of quarter-end

steps.label: Access requested
steps.detail: Manager requests a named role through ITSM (never 'same as another user'), with a business justification for sensitive roles such as compensation, payroll and ER case data.

steps.label: Check role against SoD matrix
steps.detail: The HRIS role owner checks the request against the SoD matrix: no user may combine hire/terminate, pay change and payroll approval, or bank change and payroll release.
steps.control: SoD conflict check before provisioning

steps.label: SoD conflict?
steps.detail: Decide whether the requested role creates a conflict with the user's existing access.

steps.label: Approve mitigation or reject
steps.detail: The Controller approves a time-bound exception with a compensating control (independent review of that user's transactions) or rejects the request.

steps.label: Provision via identity platform
steps.detail: IT provisions through Okta and ServiceNow; HRIS mover and leaver events adjust access automatically. Admin accounts are separate from daily accounts, and no global HRIS admin role sits with China- or Hong Kong-resident staff (DOJ Data Security Program).

steps.label: Align payroll portal roles
steps.detail: Payroll confirms that provider-side roles mirror internal approvals and extracts the provider user list for the UAR.

steps.label: Run quarterly access review
steps.detail: Role owners and managers certify every user's access in Darwinbox, Greenhouse, payroll and the equity platform, with completeness evidence for user lists; removals are executed within 5 business days.
steps.control: Quarterly UAR with completeness evidence for user listings

steps.label: SOX testing & deficiencies
steps.detail: Internal Audit and the external auditor test the controls; deficiencies are logged, remediated and evaluated for SOX 404 severity.

steps.label: Quarter certified
steps.detail: Sign-offs are archived and metrics reported to the SOX steering committee.

controls.control: SoD conflict check before provisioning, with Controller-approved mitigation for any exception
Quarterly user access review across HR, payroll and equity systems
Leaver access removed the same day, driven by the Darwinbox termination event
Monthly review of privileged-access and configuration-change logs

kpis.name: UARs completed on time
kpis.why: Late reviews are a common SOX deficiency

kpis.name: SoD conflicts without approved mitigation
kpis.why: An unmitigated conflict is a fraud path through payroll

kpis.name: Leaver access removed within 24 hours
kpis.why: Stale access is both a SOX and a trade-secret risk

considerations: 'Clone this user' requests spread excess access; insist on designed roles.
Use field-level security for sensitive data (medical, demographic, ER case notes), not just module-level access.
Include implementation partners and vendor support accounts in the UAR; they are often forgotten.
US administrators viewing China employee data is a PIPL cross-border transfer, and China-resident administrators viewing US data can be a DOJ Data Security Program issue; design regional roles.
Auditors will test completeness and accuracy of the user lists you review, so keep the extraction evidence.

variations.when: Emergency access during payroll close
variations.how: Time-boxed firefighter access, logged, and reviewed the next business day by someone independent.

variations.when: Small country HR team where one person enters and approves
variations.how: Compensating control: HQ Payroll independently reviews that country's payroll variance report every cycle.

variations.when: System implementation or upgrade
variations.how: Role redesign and SoD testing before go-live, with change-management approvals retained.

countries.us: SOX 404 makes HRIS, payroll and equity-system access part of ICFR, and auditors expect quarterly UARs and SoD. The DOJ Data Security Program restricts giving covered persons access to bulk US employee data, so global admin roles must not sit with China- or Hong Kong-resident staff.
countries.us-ca: The CCPA requires reasonable security for HR data; demographic data for pay data reporting must be stored separately from personnel files (SB 464), and medical information kept confidential (CMIA).
countries.ca: BC PIPA requires reasonable security arrangements for employee personal information (s.34; verify), and access to Canadian medical and accommodation files should be restricted to those who need it.
countries.in: Until DPDP applies, the SPDI Rules require reasonable security practices (ISO 27001 qualifies); from 13 May 2027 DPDP requires security safeguards and breach reporting, and CERT-In requires cyber incidents to be reported within 6 hours.
countries.tw: PDPA Art. 27 requires security maintenance measures (access control, audits, incident plan), with fines up to NT$15M for failures not corrected.
countries.cn: PIPL requires operating permissions for staff who handle personal information (Art. 51); US-based administrators accessing China employee data is a cross-border transfer needing a legal basis, notice and consent unless the HR-management exemption genuinely applies.

processes.name: Human capital reporting & disclosure
processes.summary: Produces governed workforce metrics for the 10-K human capital section, the proxy, customer and investor questionnaires (RBA) and statutory reports, using a metric dictionary, locked snapshots, data lineage and a CHRO sub-certification into the SOX 302 process. Good looks like every published number reconciling to a Darwinbox snapshot, stable definitions year over year, and wording that matches the programs the company actually runs.
processes.owner: HR Analytics (metrics & lineage), CHRO (sub-certification), Legal (Securities) and Finance (SEC Reporting) (disclosure)
processes.trigger: 10-K drafting calendar, proxy season, statutory report deadlines, RBA or customer questionnaires, or a material workforce event
outputs: Metric dictionary with headcount definitions (ISO 30414-aligned)
Locked snapshot and lineage binder (queries, extracts, reviewer sign-off)
Draft 10-K human capital text
CHRO sub-certification to the Disclosure Committee
Statutory and voluntary reports (CA pay data, BC pay transparency, EEO-1 while required, RBA responses)
processes.sla: Snapshot within 5 business days of fiscal year-end; draft to Disclosure Committee 30 days before filing

steps.label: Reporting calendar starts
steps.detail: Confirm disclosures and deadlines: 10-K Item 101(c), proxy, CA pay data (second Wednesday of May), BC pay transparency report (1 Nov), Canadian supply-chain report inputs (31 May), EEO-1 (pending rescission) and RBA questionnaires.

steps.label: Freeze definitions & snapshot
steps.detail: Apply the metric dictionary (e.g., headcount = active regular employees on payroll at fiscal year-end, excluding contractors and interns, stated explicitly) and take an immutable Darwinbox snapshot.
steps.control: Snapshot and definitions locked and version-controlled

steps.label: Validate data quality
steps.detail: Validate the snapshot against payroll headcount and the DS-01 reconciliation, and fix exceptions such as late-entered terminations.

steps.label: Draft metrics & narrative
steps.detail: Draft figures and text, link each figure to its query and extract in the lineage binder, and explain any change from last year's methodology.

steps.label: Legal & consistency review
steps.detail: Check wording against programs actually operated (DEI terminology, pay-equity statements), consistency across 10-K, proxy, sustainability report and careers site, and Reg FD risk.

steps.label: Sub-certify to Disclosure Committee
steps.detail: CHRO signs a sub-certification that human capital data and text are accurate and complete based on the documented process.
steps.control: CHRO sub-certification supporting SOX 302

steps.label: Disclosure Committee approves?
steps.detail: The Disclosure Committee reviews the draft and either approves or returns comments.

steps.label: File & archive evidence
steps.detail: SEC Reporting files, and HR Analytics archives the evidence binder for auditors and any SEC comment letter.

steps.label: Cycle closed
steps.detail: Post-cycle review of definition changes and lessons learned, and the next year's calendar is set.

raci.activity: Statutory workforce reports (CA pay data, BC pay transparency, EEO-1)

controls.control: Every disclosed metric traced to a locked snapshot and query with reviewer sign-off
CHRO sub-certification before Disclosure Committee approval
Legal review of wording against programs actually operated

kpis.name: Disclosed metrics with complete lineage
kpis.why: Required to support SOX 302 certifications

kpis.name: Post-filing corrections
kpis.why: Corrections undermine credibility and may require amendments

kpis.name: Methodology changes explained
kpis.why: Unexplained changes invite SEC and investor questions

considerations: Item 101(c) is principles-based: disclose what management actually uses to run the business; aspirational statements create Rule 10b-5 exposure.
State headcount definitions explicitly (contractors, interns, employees on leave, acquired staff) and keep them stable.
EEO-1 is still on the books while rescission is pending, and California pay data reporting continues regardless (23 SOC-based categories from the 2027 report).
Align DEI wording across all public documents with current programs; inconsistent statements become evidence in discrimination, False Claims Act or securities claims.
RBA customer audits compare stated policies with lab working hours and contractor practices; use the same dictionary for those responses.

variations.when: Material workforce event (RIF, export-control limits on hiring, key-talent loss)
variations.how: Brief the Disclosure Committee for risk factors, MD&A or 8-K timing, and coordinate WARN and employee communications.

variations.when: Customer RBA audit or questionnaire
variations.how: Answer from the same dictionary and snapshot, with Legal review of any policy statements.

variations.when: Voluntary publication of EEO-1 or diversity data
variations.how: Legal decides whether to publish and the methodology is documented and kept consistent year to year.

countries.us: Reg S-K Item 101(c) requires headcount and a material description of human capital measures, covered by SOX 302 certifications. The EEOC proposed rescinding EEO-1 in July 2026, but filing duties stand until a final rule, and the 2025 collection had not opened as of September 2026.
countries.us-ca: Employers with 100+ employees file the CRD pay data report by the second Wednesday of May (12 May 2027 next), moving to 23 SOC-based job categories with mandatory exempt-status fields under SB 464; demographic data must be stored separately from personnel files.
countries.ca: Employers with 50+ BC employees must publish a pay transparency report by 1 Nov 2026 and annually after. The Canadian entity may need to supply inputs for a forced-labour supply-chain report due 31 May (verify coverage).
countries.in: The Indian subsidiary's Board report must disclose POSH complaint statistics and maternity-benefit compliance (Companies (Accounts) Rules amended July 2025; verify scope).
countries.tw: Private employers with 67+ employees must meet the 1% disability employment quota or pay into the fund, and the Taiwan entity's articles must state an employee-compensation percentage of profit (Company Act Art. 235-1); keep headcount definitions consistent with these filings.
countries.cn: No statutory human capital disclosure applies to the WFOE, but exporting employee-level data for group reporting relies on the PIPL HR-management exemption, so send aggregated metrics where possible.

processes.name: HR vendor & AI tool onboarding
processes.summary: Gate for every new HR vendor and every AI or automated-decision tool (resume screeners, assessments, attrition models, monitoring, chatbots), including AI features switched on in Darwinbox or Greenhouse. It covers privacy impact assessment, security review, bias audit, AI-law compliance, cross-border transfer and DOJ Data Security Program screening before contract signature. Good looks like no HR tool touching employee data before approval, and every decision tool having bias testing, notices and a real human-review path.
processes.owner: People Ops (HR tech intake), Legal / Privacy (assessments & AI compliance), Security (vendor risk), Finance / Procurement (contracting)
processes.trigger: Request to buy or enable a new HR system, vendor or AI feature, or a material change in how an existing tool processes data
outputs: Intake questionnaire and data map
Privacy impact assessment (DPIA / CPPA risk assessment / PIPL PIPIA)
Security review and restricted-party / DSP screening result
Bias audit results and ADS/ADMT notice and appeal design
Signed contract with DPA and cross-border terms
Entry in the HR tool and AI register
processes.sla: Standard vendors 20 business days intake-to-decision; high-risk AI or decision tools 40 business days

steps.label: Tool or vendor request
steps.detail: Requester submits purpose, data categories, countries, decisions supported, AI or automation features and planned integration with Darwinbox or Greenhouse.

steps.label: Assign risk tier
steps.detail: Tier 1: tools that support hiring, promotion, pay, discipline or termination decisions, employee monitoring, sensitive data (health, biometrics) or China/India data. Tier 2: other employee data. Tier 3: no personal data.

steps.label: Security & vendor risk review
steps.detail: Review SOC 2 Type II or ISO 27001 reports, penetration tests, data location, sub-processors, SSO and MFA, encryption and breach terms.

steps.label: Restricted-party & DSP screen
steps.detail: Screen vendor and sub-processors against the Entity List, SDN and DOJ covered-persons lists, and confirm no China-resident vendor staff get access to bulk US employee data.
steps.control: Restricted-party and covered-person screen before contract

steps.label: Privacy & AI-law assessment
steps.detail: Complete the DPIA or CPPA risk assessment, a PIPL PIPIA for China data and the transfer mechanism, then map AI duties: CRD ADS rules, NYC LL144, Illinois HB 3773, Colorado SB 26-189 and CCPA ADMT (both from 1 Jan 2027), and Ontario posting disclosure.

steps.label: Provide bias audit & documentation
steps.detail: Vendor supplies an independent bias audit (selection or impact ratios by sex and race/ethnicity), model documentation, deletion capability and accommodation alternatives for candidates.

steps.label: Approve, condition or reject?
steps.detail: Legal, Security and People Ops decide jointly; conditions can include mandatory human review, disabling features, or keeping data in-region.

steps.label: Contract with DPA terms
steps.detail: Procurement signs with a DPA (CCPA service-provider terms, transfer clauses, PIPL standard contract where needed), audit rights and a duty to notify material model or feature changes.

steps.label: Register tool & set notices
steps.detail: Add the tool to the register with owner, retention, candidate and employee notices, opt-out or appeal workflow, and an annual re-review and bias-audit date.
steps.control: No production data until register entry and approvals are complete

steps.label: Decision communicated
steps.detail: Requester is notified; rejected tools are logged with reasons.

controls.control: No production employee data flows before approvals and register entry (SSO integration gated)
controls.evidence: Register entry and ITSM integration ticket

controls.control: Annual bias audit for every decision tool, with published summary where NYC LL144 applies
Restricted-party and covered-person screening before contract signature
Contract includes DPA and AI change-notification clause

kpis.name: HR tools in register with current assessments
kpis.why: Unregistered tools are where shadow AI risk lives

kpis.name: Decision tools with bias audit under 12 months old
kpis.why: Required by NYC LL144 and central to FEHA defenses

kpis.name: Intake-to-decision cycle time
kpis.why: A slow gate drives teams to bypass it

considerations: AI features switched on inside existing tools (Greenhouse, Darwinbox) are new processing and go through the gate.
Under California's CRD rules the vendor is the employer's agent; contract terms do not transfer liability, so test outcomes yourself.
Human review must be meaningful (authority, information and time to disagree); a reviewer who always accepts the score is not a safeguard.
Productivity or telemetry monitoring of engineers can require a CPPA risk assessment and PIPL, DPDP and Taiwan PDPA notices.
Keep ADS inputs and outputs for 4 years in California, and configure retention before go-live (DS-03).

variations.when: Tool with no decision role (e.g., scheduling assistant)
variations.how: Tier 2 or 3 path: privacy notice and security review only.

variations.when: Tool processing China employee data
variations.how: PIPIA, preference for in-China processing, and a standard contract filing or documented HR-management exemption before any transfer.

variations.when: Candidates in New York City in scope
variations.how: LL144 bias audit published and candidate notice at least 10 business days before use.

countries.us: NYC Local Law 144 requires an annual independent bias audit, a published summary and 10 business days' notice before using an automated employment decision tool; Illinois requires notice of AI use (HB 3773) and Colorado SB 26-189 adds notice and adverse-decision explanation duties from 1 Jan 2027. The DOJ Data Security Program (28 CFR 202) restricts vendor agreements giving covered persons access to bulk US sensitive personal data.
countries.us-ca: CRD ADS regulations (effective 1 Oct 2025) make discriminatory ADS outcomes FEHA violations, treat vendors as agents and require 4-year retention of ADS data. CPPA risk assessments already apply to ADMT and employee monitoring, and ADMT pre-use notice, opt-out or appeal and access duties start 1 Jan 2027.
countries.ca: Ontario postings must disclose AI use in screening, assessment or selection (since 1 Jan 2026), and BC PIPA requires notice of purposes. Quebec Law 25 requires a privacy impact assessment before transfers outside Quebec and notice of decisions based exclusively on automated processing.
countries.in: Until DPDP duties start on 13 May 2027, the SPDI Rules require written consent for sensitive data and reasonable security. Transfers to the US are allowed unless the government restricts the destination, and contracts should anticipate DPDP processor obligations.
countries.tw: Disclose vendor processing and cross-border transfers in the PDPA notice and bind vendors to security maintenance measures; health and other sensitive data need written consent or a statutory basis.
countries.cn: Entrusted processing, automated decision-making and cross-border transfers each require a PIPIA kept 3 years, and transfers need the HR-management exemption, a standard contract filing, certification or a CAC assessment depending on volume. Facial-recognition tools need separate consent, a non-biometric alternative and CAC filing above 100,000 individuals.

processes.name: Employment verification requests
processes.summary: Responds to employee and third-party requests to verify employment, income or service (lenders, landlords, background-check firms, immigration, government agencies) and issues statutory service, relieving and termination certificates, disclosing only what is authorized. Good looks like third-party verifications within 2 business days, written consent on file for anything beyond dates and title, and statutory certificates always on time.
processes.owner: People Ops (verification desk), Legal (subpoenas & government requests)
processes.trigger: Third-party verification request, employee request for a verification, service or experience letter, or a statutory certificate trigger at separation
outputs: Verification response (dates and title; pay only with written consent)
Employee authorization record
Statutory certificates (Taiwan LSA Art. 19 service certificate, Karnataka service certificate, China termination certificate)
Verification request log
processes.sla: Third-party verifications 2 business days; employee letters 3 business days; statutory certificates by local deadline (Karnataka 7 days from request; China at termination)

steps.label: Request received
steps.detail: Requests come through Darwinbox self-service (employee letters), the verification inbox or a third-party verification service.

steps.label: Redirect reference calls
steps.detail: Managers do not verify employment or pay; they redirect callers to People Ops under POL-56. Personal references are allowed only with HR guidance and a disclaimer.

steps.label: What is being asked?
steps.detail: Classify the request: dates and title only, pay or other personal data, or legal process (subpoena, court order, agency).

steps.label: Provide written consent
steps.detail: Employee signs an authorization for pay or other details (lender, landlord, visa application); People Ops confirms it is genuine.

steps.label: Handle legal process
steps.detail: Legal reviews subpoenas, court orders and law-enforcement or agency requests, notifies the employee where permitted, and responds within the legal deadline.

steps.label: Prepare & send response
steps.detail: Generate from a Darwinbox template with data as of today, send through a secure channel, and issue statutory certificates in the local language (Chinese for China and Taiwan).
steps.control: Pay disclosed only with consent on file

steps.label: Log & close
steps.detail: Log requester, data disclosed, consent reference and date.

controls.control: Compensation or other personal data disclosed only with the employee's signed authorization or legal compulsion
controls.evidence: E-signature authorization linked to the log

controls.control: Statutory certificate deadlines tracked per request and separation

kpis.name: Third-party verifications within 2 business days
kpis.why: Delays hold up employees' loans, leases and visas

kpis.name: Statutory certificates issued on time
kpis.why: Karnataka, Taiwan and China certificates carry legal consequences

considerations: A neutral policy (dates and title) limits defamation and negligent-referral risk; managers are the usual leak.
Automated verification services receive payroll data; confirm the contract treats them as a service provider and that employees are told (CCPA 'no sale' of HR data).
Never put separation reasons or investigation outcomes in certificates (Taiwan bans unrequested adverse remarks; China should omit negative reasons).
Immigration letters must match HRIS and visa filings exactly; route discrepancies to Immigration before sending.

variations.when: Former employee asks an ex-manager for a reference
variations.how: Allow a personal reference only with HR guidance and a disclaimer, or give the neutral verification.

variations.when: Verification for an employee on leave or under investigation
variations.how: Confirm current status factually (active employee) and never mention leave reasons or investigations.

variations.when: Unemployment or benefit agency request (EDD, Service Canada, Taiwan separation certificate)
variations.how: People Ops responds within the agency's deadline with the statutory form and reason code.

countries.us: There is no federal duty to give references, but some states require service letters on request (e.g., MN within 10 working days; MO, KS, NV; verify). FCRA governs requests made by consumer reporting agencies for a prospective employer.
countries.us-ca: Truthful, good-faith references are privileged (Civ. Code 47(c)), but statements made to prevent someone getting work are prohibited (LC 1050-1053); former employees may also request personnel files (30 days) and payroll records (21 days).
countries.ca: Disclose only what the employee has authorized, since BC PIPA limits use of employee information to managing employment (verify for third-party verifications), and file ROEs with Service Canada on the statutory timeline.
countries.in: In Karnataka, issue a service certificate within 7 days of the employee's request (2026 amendment) and never retain original certificates; relieving and experience letters should not be withheld to enforce notice.
countries.tw: On request, issue a service certificate (LSA Art. 19) with dates and position and no adverse remarks the employee did not ask for; for Art. 11/13 terminations and employer-initiated separations, issue the involuntary separation certificate for unemployment benefits.
countries.cn: Issue a termination certificate at separation stating contract term, termination date, position and years of service (LCL Art. 50), omitting negative reasons; giving employee data to prospective employers or background vendors needs separate consent (PIPL Art. 23).

processes.name: Policy lifecycle governance
processes.summary: Governs how HR policies are proposed, drafted, localized, legally reviewed, consulted on, approved, published, attested, reviewed and retired across a five-level hierarchy: global policy > regional standard > country addendum > procedure > guideline. Every document lives in one register with an owner, version, citations and review date, and local enforceability steps (China democratic procedure, Taiwan work-rule filing, India standing orders) gate the effective date. Good looks like zero overdue reviews, 98%+ attestation within 30 days, and the ability to show in minutes what any policy said on any date and who acknowledged it.
processes.owner: People Ops - HR Policy & Governance (process), domain policy owners (content), Legal (review), CHRO (approval)
processes.trigger: Proposed new policy or change (law change from the research watchlist, audit finding, incident trend, business change, employee feedback) or a policy's annual review date
outputs: Policy register entry (ID, tier, owner, version, effective and review dates, citations)
Draft in T-POLICY with redline and change log
Country legal review memos and addenda
Consultation and filing evidence (China, Taiwan, India, unions)
Approved, translated and published versions with archived predecessors
Attestation completion records and quarterly governance metrics
processes.sla: Standard change 45 business days intake-to-publication; legally mandated change live before the statutory effective date; every policy reviewed at least annually

steps.label: Change proposed or review due
steps.detail: The intake form captures trigger, affected policies, countries, urgency and requester; the register automatically flags policies whose review date falls in the next 60 days and watchlist items with effective dates.

steps.label: Triage & set hierarchy tier
steps.detail: Governance lead assigns the tier (global policy, regional standard, country addendum, procedure or guideline), the accountable owner and a target date. Local legal deltas go in addenda; the global text is never forked by country.
steps.control: Every document has one owner and one tier in the register

steps.label: Draft in T-POLICY
steps.detail: Owner drafts purpose, scope, definitions, provisions, roles, exceptions, related policies, addendum placeholders and change log in plain language, separating mandatory 'must' statements from guidance.

steps.label: Gather stakeholder input
steps.detail: HRBPs and country HR leads test operability and local practice; Finance, Security, Trade Compliance and E&C comment where relevant, and comments are logged against the draft.

steps.label: Legal review per country
steps.detail: Employment counsel reviews the global text and each addendum for enforceability: NLRA Section 7 and Rule 21F-17 carve-outs (US), 2 CCR 11023 content (CA), ESA and OHSA required policies (Ontario), the Labour Codes (India), LSA (Taiwan) and LCL (China), and produces addendum text and a review memo.
steps.control: Legal review memo per affected country on file before approval

steps.label: Consultation or filing needed?
steps.detail: Legal decides whether the change touches pay, hours, leave, discipline or other vital interests (China), work-rule content (Taiwan, 30+ employees), standing orders (India, 300+ workers) or union-bargained terms.

steps.label: Consult & record consents
steps.detail: China: discussion with the employee congress or all employees, then consultation with the union or representatives, with feedback and responses recorded. Taiwan: table at the labor-management meeting where consent is needed. India: standing-order and GRC steps. Unionized units: bargain.
steps.control: Consultation evidence attached to the register before approval

steps.label: Translate & localize
steps.detail: Professional translation into Simplified Chinese (China) and Traditional Chinese (Taiwan), each prevailing locally; French for any Quebec staff; and CA FEHA policy languages spoken by 10%+ of a facility's workforce. Legal terms are back-checked.

steps.label: Approved under the matrix?
steps.detail: Global policies: CHRO, plus the Board or its committee for the Code, clawback and insider trading. Regional standards and addenda: regional HR head with Legal. Procedures: policy owner. Approvers see the redline, legal memos and consultation evidence.

steps.label: File with authorities
steps.detail: Taiwan: file work rules with the local labor authority (Science Park Bureau for Hsinchu Science Park) and post them. India: certify or register standing orders where applicable. Ontario: record preparation and change dates on the disconnecting and e-monitoring policies.

steps.label: Publish & version
steps.detail: Publish on the policy portal with version, effective date and change summary; archive the prior version read-only; update Darwinbox handbook links and cross-references; retire superseded documents.
steps.control: Published version matches register version; prior versions archived

steps.label: Assign attestation & training
steps.detail: Assign attestation to the in-scope population in the LMS (new hires within 30 days; changes within 30 days of publication) and run manager briefings or training for material changes (PD-06).

steps.label: Read & acknowledge
steps.detail: Employees acknowledge by LMS or e-signature. In China the signed acknowledgment is the publicity evidence needed for enforceability, and Ontario employees receive disconnecting and e-monitoring policy copies within 30 days.

steps.label: Track completion & escalate
steps.detail: Weekly completion reports go to HRBPs; non-completers are escalated to managers at 30 days and Dept Heads at 45 days.

steps.label: Report metrics & run review calendar
steps.detail: The register drives the annual review calendar, and quarterly metrics (overdue reviews, attestation, exceptions granted, policy-related ER cases) go to the CHRO.

steps.label: Cycle closed; next review set
steps.detail: Next review date is set (at most 12 months; Ontario OHSA violence and harassment policies at least annually) and the intake ticket is closed.

controls.control: Quarterly register completeness check: every policy has owner, tier, version, citations, effective and review dates
Legal review memo per affected country before approval
China, Taiwan and India consultation or filing evidence complete before the local effective date
controls.evidence: Minutes, acknowledgments and filing receipts in the register

controls.control: Approval under the matrix with redline retained
Only the current version is live; prior versions archived read-only for the retention period
Attestation completion monitored with escalation at 30 and 45 days
Annual scan of policies and templates for NLRA Section 7 and Rule 21F-17 issues
controls.evidence: Legal scan memo and remediation log

kpis.name: Policies past review date
kpis.why: Stale policies are unenforceable in practice and a common audit finding

kpis.name: Attestation completion within 30 days
kpis.why: Acknowledgment is the evidence needed in discipline and litigation

kpis.name: Intake-to-publication cycle time
kpis.why: A slow cycle pushes teams to publish unofficial guidance

kpis.name: Local enforceability steps complete before effective date
kpis.why: A China handbook without democratic procedure cannot support dismissals

kpis.name: ER cases citing unclear or conflicting policy
kpis.why: Tests whether policies are usable, not just approved

considerations: Hierarchy discipline: global policies state principles and minimums, addenda carry local deltas, and where local law is stricter the addendum wins; forking the global text by country makes version control impossible.
Publication is not enforceability: in China an unconsulted handbook does not support Art. 39 dismissals and in Taiwan unfiled work rules weaken discipline, so effective dates may differ by country.
US handbooks need an at-will disclaimer, Section 7-safe wording and Rule 21F-17 carve-outs, and should not make progressive discipline contractual.
Control translations with a prevailing-language clause per country and a shared translation memory, and make sure employees can understand rules that will be used against them.

Litigants and auditors ask what a policy said on a given date and who acknowledged it; keep every version and acknowledgment for the retention period (Ontario policies 3 years after they cease to apply).
Keep procedures separate from policy so operational changes do not trigger consultation or filing, but in China a procedure that affects vital interests still needs democratic procedure.
Connect the research watchlist to the register (e.g., CA SB 947, the Cal/OSHA workplace violence standard, Taiwan PDPC effective date) so legal changes open tickets automatically.
Avoid attestation fatigue: bundle an annual attestation (Code plus key policies) and reserve mid-year attestations for material changes.
Run a logged exception process with owner approval and expiry dates; an exception for an executive officer may be a Code waiver that must be disclosed.

variations.when: Urgent legal change with a near effective date (e.g., California laws effective 1 January)
variations.how: Expedited path: Legal drafts the addendum, employees get an interim notice, and the full cycle follows within 60 days.

variations.when: China change that reduces entitlements (e.g., Shanghai sick pay after the 15 Aug 2026 lapse)
variations.how: Full democratic procedure, a reasonableness and grandfathering analysis, and Legal sign-off before announcement.

variations.when: Taiwan entity reaches 30 employees
variations.how: Adopt and file work rules within 30 days, and adopt harassment and bullying prevention measures and disciplinary rules.

variations.when: Ontario headcount is 25+ on 1 January
variations.how: Disconnecting-from-work and electronic-monitoring policies in place by 1 March, with copies to employees within 30 days.

variations.when: Acquisition integration
variations.how: Map acquired policies into the register, keep acquired terms until harmonization is consulted, and avoid unilateral changes that risk constructive dismissal in Canada.

variations.when: Board-level policy (Code of Conduct, clawback, insider trading)
variations.how: Board or committee approval, public posting of the Code (Nasdaq 5610) and filing of the insider trading policy as a 10-K exhibit (Item 408(b)).

variations.when: Policy applies to a subset only (e.g., sales compensation governance)
variations.how: Managed as a procedure or standard with owner approval, but still registered, versioned and attested by the in-scope group.

countries.us: Nasdaq Rule 5610 requires a publicly available code of conduct with disclosed executive waivers, and a handbook that describes benefits must include FMLA rights (50+ employees). Review every work rule against Stericycle while it remains binding and include Rule 21F-17 protected-rights carve-outs. Remote employees need their work state's required policies and notices (e.g., state sick leave, NY electronic-monitoring acknowledgment).
countries.us-ca: The FEHA EEO and harassment policy must list all protected categories, include a complaint route that bypasses the supervisor, be distributed with acknowledgment, and be translated into any language spoken by 10%+ of a facility's workforce (2 CCR 11023). Handbooks must describe CFRA and PDL rights, and stand-alone requirements include the IIPP, WVPP, lactation policy and the annual SB 294 Know Your Rights notice by 1 February. The CCPA notice must state retention per category, so keep policy and retention-schedule changes in sync.
countries.ca: Ontario employers with 25+ employees on 1 January need written disconnecting-from-work and electronic-monitoring policies by 1 March, copies to employees within 30 days, and retention for 3 years after a policy ceases to apply. OHSA violence and harassment policies must be posted at 6+ workers and reviewed at least annually, and BC bullying and harassment policies must also be reviewed annually. Any Quebec staff need French versions under Bill 96.
countries.in: Establishments with 300+ workers must certify standing orders or adopt the model standing orders under the IR Code; the Karnataka IT/ITeS exemption (to June 2029) is conditional and its status under the Codes needs confirmation. The POSH policy and IC details must be displayed in English and Kannada, an equal opportunity policy for persons with disabilities must be published (RPwD Act s.21), and the holiday list displayed before the year starts.
countries.tw: At 30+ employees, work rules covering hours, leave, wages, discipline and termination must be filed with the local labor authority (the Science Park Bureau for Hsinchu Science Park sites) within 30 days and posted, and global policies are not enforceable locally unless incorporated. GEEA harassment and OSH Act bullying prevention measures, complaint procedures and disciplinary rules must be adopted and published at 30+ employees. The Traditional Chinese version is the one courts and inspectors rely on.
countries.cn: Rules on pay, hours, leave, safety, discipline and training are enforceable only after democratic procedure (discussion with the employee congress or all employees, then consultation with the union or representatives) and publicity with signed acknowledgment (LCL Art. 4; SPC Interpretation (I) Art. 50). Changes that reduce entitlements face heightened reasonableness scrutiny. Make Chinese the prevailing language and keep the consultation file as evidence.
